डॉ. किरिट पी. सोलंकी (अहमदाबाद) :आजकल क्लाइमेट चेंज सबसे बड़ा सवाल है । पूरे विश्व में पर्यावरण की जो स्थिति पैदा हुई है, वह बहुत ही निराशाजनक स्थिति है । आजकल पर्यावरण का जो विनाश हो रहा है, जंगल को जिस तरह समाप्त किया जाता है उसके लिए सबसे बड़ी जवाबदेही विकसित देशों की वजह से हुई है । पूरे विश्व के पर्यावरण को प्रदू­िात करने का कार्य विकसित देशों ने किया है । उसके लिए भारत जैसे देशों की जवाबदेही बहुत कम है । मेरा सरकार से निवेदन है कि सरकार को इस बात पर जोर देना चाहिए ।

पर्यावरण क्लीयरेंस देने के बारे में हमारी सरकार ने जो लचीलापनता अपनाई है इसकी वजह से पर्यावरण एवं विकास का संतुलन बना है इसके लिए मैं सरकार को धन्यवाद देता हूं ।

जहां तक बायो-मेडिकल वेस्ट कानून का सवाल है, यह बहुत महत्वपूर्ण वि­ाय है । इस वि­ाय में कॉमन बायोमेडिकल फसेलीटियोंस का सवाल है गुजरात में दो कंपनियां बहुत अच्छा कार्य कर रही हैं । मगर अच्छे कार्य करने वाली सीबीएमडब्ल्यूटीएफ को अलग-अलग प्रकार क नए प्रावधानों के लिए मजबूर किया जाता है । उन सीबीएमडब्ल्यूटीएफ को आदर्श गाइड लाइंस के लिए सख्ताई किया जाता है । मेरा सरकार से निवेदन है कि उनमें लचीलापन लाना चाहिए तथा अच्छे कार्य करने वाली सीबीएमडब्ल्यूटीएफ की सराहना चाहिए ।

भारत की संस्कृति पर्यावरण का हमेशा सम्मान करती है । मेरा मानना है कि भारतीय संस्कृति ही पर्यावरण को बचाने का उपाय है ।

*SHRI NALIN KUMAR KATEEL (DAKSHINA KANNADA): With regard to implementation of Kasturirangan report on the Western Ghats the government should take the views of local people before demarcation of ecologically-sensitive areas in their respective areas as suggested by the Committee report.

With regard to create a clean and sustainable environment, the government should frame guidelines to ensure that all the cities and towns should strictly adhere to handle their own garbage, liquid and solid waste. However, there is not proper planning made by the agencies and the authorities have not shown keen interest to take real-life challenges into account while preparing guidelines. This is not about making our cities smarter in terms of posh buildings and malls but about sustainable living. This can be possible with better planning and strict implementation of the same. 

As far as Climate change is concerned, from school going children to Professor, a Layman to a leader, everyone is aware of the effects of the climate change. The country needs to develop and adopt innovative solutions to mitigate the effects of climate change. The union Government should fix a target and direct all the state government s to introduce atleast one climate change plan every year.

With regard to find out the solution to curb the increasing pollutions, the government should take some effective measures for classification of industrial units in a scientific manner. As we are aware that air pollutants, effluents and nature of waste- hazardous or otherwise- produced are part of an industrial unit's operations, the industrial units should be classified as per the severity of pollution produced by them. The government should put in a proper mechanism to conduct periodical review of the compliance of the standard norms of pollution.

In order to save fresh water industrial units should be asked to use treated water and directed to introduce zero liquid discharge system in the industries.

I welcome the proposal of the government to consider declaring at least one Biodiversity Heritage Site in 2015-16. It is very important step in order to conservation and preservation of biological resources of the particular regions. The government should put in place a transparent and effective mechanism for access to biological resources in all states and regions. There is also need to take steps to assess the animal population of various species to consider the option of their population management.

I would like to point out that the environmental governance institutions in our country are not effectively functioning to preserve and conserve the environment and forest resources. It is evident from the style of functioning of pollution control boards and wildlife trusts. The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) has insufficient coordination with State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs). Other constraints like lack of civil administrative authority, ineffective accountability, lack of stakeholder awareness, high levels of corruption and inadequate monitoring skills remain prevalent in the implementation of the various facts related to it.

As a result, forest destruction is rampant in the country. Illegal cutting and selling off timber, firewood shortage and consequential soil erosion is keeping the productivity of Indian agricultural lands low. Crop lands have expanded on to marginal lands and have reduced grazing lands. With unemployment and landlessness growing, even pro-forest tribal groups are looking to monetize forestry resources. Keeping all these shortcomings in the existing forest laws in view the Union Government should bring an effective and modern law to strike a balance between development and environment to protect all the stakeholders including forest dwellers.

SHRI T. RADHAKRISHNAN (VIRUDHUNAGAR) : Hon. Deputy-Speaker, Sir, environment needs to be protected from all kinds of pollution. We need to inculcate a sense of protecting environment in our younger generation. This is necessary because various kinds of pollution affect our air, water and sky resulting in change in climate. This comes in the way of our getting a regular rainfall. This affects the availability of water which is vital for our lives. 

Pollution in our river system, both by allowing the flow of human waste as well as industrial waste is a big challenge. We have Pollution Control Board. A number of laws and rules have been framed by all the Governments over the years. But still the amount of pollution is on an increase with rising population. That is why we have a Ministry dedicated to environment, which also looks after the conservation of forests. This Ministry also extends its services as a mouthpiece of the Government in the world forums where climate change is a much talked about matter. 

I wish to congratulate the Government for the lead it has taken among the developing countries with regard to the measures taken about the dent in the ozone layer. The world is today worrying about change in climate world over. The developed countries, which were emitting volumes of toxic gases all these years, have started dictating terms to the developing countries like India. We are compelled to reduce the use of fossil fuels. This will naturally affect our industrial activities in a big way. 

In the name of reduction in carbon rates, that is, gas emission due to use of coal, petrol and natural gas, many restrictions are being imposed upon us. As this will slow down our economic progress, we are on the look out for alternative energy sources.

When it comes to environment, it is a part of our life cycle – one connected with the other. For instance, deforestation and depletion of forest cover have affected the rain pattern. This also adds to the misery that results out of climate change. Forests can survive only when we allow the wild animals there to survive. Only when the green cover is protected, the survival of human race and sustainability of human life is possible. 

Having pointed out the inter-relation within the three responsibilities this Ministry has been entrusted with, I may now try to go into the budgetary allocation for this Ministry. The actual allocation for this Ministry in 2013-14 was Rs.2,256 crore, whereas the Revised Estimate ended up as Rs.1,764 crore. When the existing expenses in the face of price rise have increased manifold, this year’s allocation is just Rs.1,681 crore. 

I do not understand how the Ministry will be able to train its manpower to protect our forest cover or the wildlife. I also fail to understand the scaling down of allocation for research in this field for a vast country like ours with varying geographical conditions and the second largest population in the world. 

Zoological parks in a tropical country like ours must have improvised modern facilities to carefully protect the animal species that are parked there and to nurture them. Unfortunately, the allocation for Central Zoo Authority has been cut drastically from Rs. 26.5 crore to Rs. 5.88 crore. Here, I would like to point out the compassionate gesture of our guiding spirit puratchi thalaivi Amma in conducting annual camps for all the temple elephants in Tamil Nadu. This annual camp held in Mudumalai Sanctuary is like the annual health camp for those animals that remain in the temples in the midst of the human population throughout the year. Hon. Minister of Environment and Forests, Shri Prakash Javadekar was highly appreciating recently this kind of continued gesture of our leader in taking care of the wild animals, especially the elephants. I recall his paying rich encomium to our beloved leader Amma in the Consultative Committee meeting held at Bandipur Forests in Karnataka. 

When it comes to environmental education, training and extension, it is needless to say that such programmes with enhanced allocation must continue in the wake of rise in population. What was Rs. 47 crore in 2013-14 was actually brought down to Rs. 30 crore in 2014-15 by this Government. More than punitive measures for violation and damage control at a huge cost, creating awareness towards the protection of environment is necessary. 

I fail to understand the overall trend of the Union Government to slice down the fund allocation for strategically important Ministries, like the Ministry of Environment which has to tackle various environmental issues. I am afraid that it will be too much to expect from the industries. 

Recruiting adequate manpower, providing needed training with essential equipment at their disposal and ensuring coordinated action in protecting forest wealth, especially in the inter-State border areas, is necessary. The mismanagement in this area by the Centre has resulted in the recent tragic incident that happened in the Seshachalam Forest in Chittoor District of Andhra Pradesh bordering Tamil Nadu. I expect that the Union Minister currently holding the responsibility will evolve a suitable plan of action to avoid the recurrence of such unpleasant incidents. I hope that the Minister will not shirk his responsibility stating that those forests come under the purview of the State Government. 

Before I could conclude, let me draw the attention of the Union Government to evolve a national policy to overcome the problems created by small and medium scale industrial units in paper and cardboard manufacturing. The effluents from these units are polluting both air and water in the vicinity. In the proposed new GST regime manufacturing States will be getting less revenue. This, in reality, will mean that the State Government will be more hard-pressed to attend to the need to protect the environment. In our Virudhunagar Constituency, the industrial waste from paper and board units causes great havoc. I would urge upon the Union Government to study the problem and to evolve a viable method to provide a centralised effluent treatment plant. Ignoring the needs of the Ministry of Environment will end in national disaster. This may not appear so before our eyes, but the destruction will be inevitable and irretrievable. Giving this word of caution let me conclude. Thank you, Sir.

श्रीमती रमा देवी (शिवहर)ः वन एवं पर्यावरण किसी भी देश के विकास एवं भवि­य के लिए बहुत ही महत्वपूर्ण घटक है। हमारे देश में सदियों पुरानी वन एवं प्रकृति के विभिन्न रूपों की पूजा एवं संरक्षण पद्धति अपनायी गयी है। व्यवसायीकरण, औद्योगिकीकरण एवं शहरीकरण के चलते वन एवं पर्यावरण पर इसका न सिर्फ हमारे देश में अपितु पूरे विश्व में प्रतिकूल प्रभाव पड़ा है। आधुनिकता एवं जनसंख्या विस्फोट ने तो वन एवं पर्यावरण को बुरी तरह से क्षति पहुंचाया है। आज जलवायु परिवर्तन, ग्लोबल वार्मिंग एवं प्रदू­ाण के चलते विश्व में करोड़ों लोग तकलीफ झेल रहे हैं। मनु­य क्या जानवर एवं पेड़-पौधे तक इस विनाश लीला से प्रभावित हुए है। यह हमारा सौभाग्य है कि हमारे देश की अदालतें वन एवं पर्यावरण मुद्दे पर शुरू से गंभीर रही है। भिन्न-भिन्न न्यायालयों के सैकड़ों फैसलों ने सरकारों को मजबूर किया कि वे वन एवं पर्यावरण की समुचित रक्षा करें।

इसके बावजूद आज वन क्षेत्र हमारे देश में घटना ही जा रहा है। पशु-पक्षी विलुप्त होते जा रहे हैं। वनों में मिलने वाले कई प्रकार के पौधे अब दिखाई नहीं देते। लालचवश हमारे देश के लोगों ने वन एवं पर्यावरण का दोहन किया है। आजादी के बाद से कांग्रेस की सरकारों ने देश की वन सम्पदा, खादानों एवं नदियों को भी नहीं बख्शा। जिसके परिणामस्वरूप हमारे देश की स्थिति वन एवं पर्यावरण के मामले में अन्य देशों की तुलना में अच्छी नहीं है।

व­ाऩ 2014 में एनडीए सरकार के आने के बाद वन एवं पर्यावरण संरक्षण पर ध्यान दिया जाने लगा है। जलवायु परिवर्तन एवं स्थायी विकास पर विश्व द्वारा किए जाने वाले नए करारों के आलोक में व­ाऩ 2015 के एक अभिप्रेरणा व­ाऩ होने की संभावना है। यह अगले 15 व­ााॉ के लिए वैश्विक समुदाय हेतु अंतर्रा­ट्रीय विकास और पर्यावरणीय नीति संबंधी कार्य सूची के पाठय़क्रम का निर्धारण करेगा। केन्द्र सरकार द्वारा जलवायु परिवर्तन के संबंध में वित्त जुटाने हेतु भारत की संस्थागत संस्था को बढ़ाया जा रहा है। हाल ही में कुछ प्रमुख पहलों में सोलर मिशन को जोर-शोर से बढ़ाया जा रहा है। इसके अतिरिक्त बजट 2014-15 की उद्घो­ाणाओं की अनुवर्ती कार्रवाई के रूप में 100 करोड़ रुपए की प्रारंभिक निधि से अनुकूल कार्यों की सहायता के लिए एवं कृ­िा, पानी, वानिकी इत्यादि जैसे क्षेत्रों में जलवायु परिवर्तन की चुनौतियों से लड़ने के लिए रा­ट्रीय अनुकूल निधि की स्थापना की गई है।

कार्बन बाजार में भारत की भागीदारी एक सफलता की कहानी है। भारत क्योटो प्रोटोकॉल के अंतर्गत स्थापित स्वच्छ विकास तंत्र (सीडीएम) की कुल सात हजार पांच सौ नवासी परियोजनाओं में से 1541 परियोजनाएं भारत के द्वारा क्रियान्वित की जा रही है। अभी तक जारी कुल प्रमाणित उत्सर्जन ह्रास (सीईआर) 1.52 बिलियन यूनिट है। जिसमें भारत का हिस्सा 191 मिलियन यूनिट का है। इसके अतिरिक्त जो 2941 परियोजनाएं अनुमोदित हुई है उससे हमारे देश में लगभग 580000 करोड़ रुपए के निवेश में सहायता मिलेगी।

केन्द्र सरकार का वन एवं पर्यावरण मंत्रालय भारत में जीव जन्तु सर्वेक्षण एवं अणवेशन में सतत् प्रयासरत है। वन प्रबंधन योजना में भी तेजी लायी जा रही है। वन्य जीव अपराध नियंत्रण ब्यूरो स्थापित किया गया है। भारतीय वन्य जीवन संस्थान, केन्द्रीय चिड़ियाघर प्राधिकरण, हाथी एवं बाघ परियोजनाओं के द्वारा वन एवं पर्यावरण मामलों पर विशे­ा ध्यान दिया जा रहा है। केन्द्रीय प्रदू­ाण नियंत्रण बोर्ड, बायो मेडिकल कचरा प्रबंधन, ई-कचरा प्रबंधन, रा­ट्रीय आर्द्र भूमि संरक्षण कार्यक्रम, रा­ट्रीय वनरोपण कार्यक्रम, पर्यावरण शिक्षा जागरूकता एवं प्रशिक्षण कार्यक्रमों के द्वारा इस क्षेत्र में आशातीत सफलता पाने की कोशिश की जा रही है। ओजोन सुरक्षा पर भी विशे­ा ध्यान दिया जा रहा है। पर्यावरण मंजूरी के लिए राज्यों को ऑनलाईन मंजूरी देने को कहा जा रहा है। प्रदू­ाण फैलाने वाले उद्योगों को रेड, ऑरेंज और ग्रीन कलर की श्रेणियों में रखने का फैसला किया गया है। हमारे प्रधानमंत्री जी हमेशा ऊर्जा क्षेत्र में आत्मनिर्भरता और आयात में कटौती पर ध्यान दे रहे है। ग्रीन एनर्जी प्रोडक्टस को पब्लिक सेक्टर बैंक पौने दो लाख करोड़ रुपए का लोन देने जा रहे है। यानि, बिजली, संकट को दूर करने में ग्रीन एनर्जी का बड़ा रोल होने वाला है। सरकार का टारगेट 2022 तक 1 लाख मेगावाट सोलर एनर्जी, 60 लाख मेगावाट विंड एनर्जी पैदा करने का है। सबसे खुशी की बात है कि 40 साल बाद हमारे देश ही नहीं पूरे विश्व में कार्बन उत्सर्जन में कमी आई है। हमारे केन्द्र सरकार का संकल्प है हरियाली की हिफाजत। केन्द्रीय ग्रामीण विकास मंत्रालय ने यह फैसला लिया है कि देशभर में फारेस्ट एरिया बढ़ाने और करीब 30 लाख परिवारों को रोजगार देने के मकसद से जो ग्रीन इंडिया मिशन की शुरूआत की गई है उसे मनरेगा से जोड़ा जाएगा। सरकार ने उद्योगपतियों से कहा है कि स्वच्छ जल, स्वच्छ हवा, स्वच्छ ऊर्जा, स्वच्छ पर्यावरण और अधिक हरियाली को केन्द्र में रखकर ही उन्हें औद्योगिक उत्पाद बनाने या बेचने चाहिए।

मुझे पूरा विश्वास है कि हमारी सरकार देश हित एवं जन हित में वन एवं पर्यावरण संबंधी मामलों को हल करेगी और अब हमारे देश से प्रदू­ाण, जलवायु परिवर्तन एवं ग्लोबल वार्मिंग जैसे नकारात्मक तत्व दूर होंगे और आदमी का जीवन खुशहाल होगा। इसमें सभी भारतीयों का साथ मिलेगा और सबका विकास होगा।

DR. MAMTAZ SANGHAMITA (BARDHMAN DURGAPUR): Thank you, hon. Deputy-Speaker, Sir. The sky, air, water, land and live inhabitants constitute our environment, and all of them are equally important to live in this world. After the world was formed, gradually the environment became congenial for life and then only from one cell different plants and animals and by further evolution process human beings came into being. They need clean water, air and also various productive animals and plants for their livelihood and for living. But due to various reasons like change in climate and natural calamities as well as with the advancement of science and urbanisation and modern life there are immense problems, which have created pollution in this world. 

15.17 hrs (Shri Konakalla Narayana Rao in the Chair) 

Now, all over the world, there is one single problem that is really worrying everybody, that is, global warming, which is due to various causes that I have already mentioned here. Among them, an important point is carbon emission in the air. Everybody is thinking about how to eliminate the carbon emission problem. 

What is the effect of global warming? It affects our health in various ways, and the main thing is that air and water is warming up. So, there is unnatural climate, untimely rain and untimely weather changes that leads to various abnormalities and loss of life. 

Another issue involved in this is reduction in forest area all over the world due to the reasons mentioned by me earlier. There is decrease in the animal world due to decrease in forest land, which is their inhabiting place, as a result, the number of animals and birds is either reducing or many are on the verge of extinction. What happens in such a situation? For example, birds are necessary for making flowers. Similarly, other animals are needed for various other things. 

The forest land cover is decreasing. There is erosion in sea and rivers due to loss of various things. The saddest part is while we are thinking about doing something to change the world environment for making it congenial to human life, there is a gross reduction in the Ministry’s budget this year in certain things. Of course, for the Prime Minister’s priority project, the Ganga Action Plan, the allocation has been increased, and also there is 100 per cent reduction in terms of taxes. My earnest request to the Minister is that along with the Ganga Action Plan, other rivers should also be saved from pollution. There should be a law to ensure that the industrial waste which now flows into rivers gets treated and the industrial effluents are not dumped in rivers, but are treated to make it pollution free.

It is sad that there is a cut in the money allocated for forest conservation. Previously, the allocation which was Rs. 5,045 crore has now been reduced to almost half, that is, to Rs. 2,099 crore. It is quite insufficient for managing wildlife in more than 650 protected areas. There is also a 15 per cent decrease in the funds allocated for Project Tiger, that is, it has been reduced from Rs. 161 crore, to Rs. 136 crore, especially when the tiger population is basically increasing in India by 30 per cent since last year. 

I am from Bengal. I must say that the unique mangroves present in Sundarbans areas as well as in Andaman are congenial for the inhabitation of Bengal tigers. We are seeing a reduction there also due to pollution in those areas, especially due to plastics, soil erosion caused by various factors and the spill of oil from launches, etc. Therefore, there should be a provision of more funds for the protection of mangroves, especially in Bengal and Andaman areas. 

Another very important treasure of our Indian Ocean is the coral reefs in Andaman and Lakshadweep Islands. Ecologically, they are very good for the fishes as well as human beings. However, due to tsunami and other factors, these coral reefs cover has been reduced. There was no provision made in this budget for the preservation of these coral reefs.

As you know, Bengal tiger is world famous and it is our national animal. However, instead of providing more funds for increasing their population, we are decreasing the budget allocation. Shri Satpathy is saying that you are trying to change it to ‘lion’, which is in the Gir Forests. As you know, you will find tigers all over India, at many places. There are eight reserve forests wherein tiger population is more and, therefore, it should remain our national animal. 

Moreover, the Standing Committee in its report has said that the budget was inadequate for controlling pollution and increasing forest cover. In Bengal, the forest cover has increased by 18 per cent; it has also increased in Andhra Pradesh, North East, etc. Forest produce is the livelihood of underprivileged persons like the Adivasis and poor people living in and around those areas. 

I would like to make a few suggestions. There should be forest preservation as forest produce is a livelihood for the people. It should be given more grants and there should be more vigilance in this regard. With regard to renewable energy, they have increased the budget, but still that is not sufficient. You should be vigilant in that respect. There should be strong action against the usage of plastic in coastal areas. Please do think about the birds that are becoming extinct in our country. Thank you.

SHRI GAURAV GOGOI (KALIABOR): The Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change must advocate on behalf of the environment and wildlife. Instead the Ministry is interested only in providing rapid clearances to big industrial projects. Around 450 industrial projects have been cleared. Yet the Ministry has not shown any concrete results on key issues such as poaching, air pollution, water degradation and declining bio-diversity. On these issues, the Ministry have only offered mere assurances. There is no Project to curb Rhino poaching. Poaching of small animals such as panglossian is continuing unabated. The polluted air in Delhi increasing the number of asthma cases in children. With so many critical challenges the budget cuts have only crippled the Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change.

*SHRI P. KUMAR (TIRUCHIRAPPALLI): The environmental issue has become an issue of public importance. It is gaining in all aspects of our life. I am glad that the government has been paying much attention to this issue whether it is conversion of forest land, pollution of river, air pollution, noise pollution, etc. The National Green Tribunal has come and are quite active now a days. I have come a cross with a news report that the government is considering to create or revise many of the existing environmental laws in consultation with the state government. It is a good idea because the environmental issues have to be dealt by the state governments and overall supervision with the union government. What I have come across that many state governments were not able to implement the directions of all the directions of the pollution control boards because of the paucity of funds. The directions of installing sewerage treatment plants is an issue because it involves huge amount of money. Therefore, it is my urge that the government should provide some sort of assistance to state governments for installation of STP.

Another issue which I would like to mention here is that the tribal people who were living in forest area, in which they were living from a period unknown. because of the rigid environmental laws, these people are deprived of many developmental activities, such as laying of roads, etc. Therefore, in the interest of the tribal people, I urge upon the government to relax some of the provisions of the environmental laws, so that for the welfare of tribal people living in the forest land, they can also enjoy some of the benefits which the people living in other areas are already enjoying. 

डॉ. वीरेन्द्र कुमार (टीकमगढ़)ः जैसा कि हम सभी जानते हैं कि पर्यावरण, वन और जलवायु परिवर्तन मंत्रालय भारत की पर्यावरण एवं वन नीति को लागू करने तथा झीलों, नदियों, इसकी जैव विविधता, वन एवं वन्य जीवों सहित देश के प्राकृतिक संसाधनों के संरक्षण तथा प्रदू­ाण रोकथाम और प्रदू­ाण कम करने के रोकथाम की देखभाल करने के लिए एक प्रमुख मंत्रालय है। मंत्रालय की नीतियों और कार्यक्रमों को लागू करने में सतत् विकास के सिद्धांत से निर्देशित होता है। मंत्रालय, संयुक्त रा­ट्र पर्यावरण कार्यक्रम, दक्षिण एशिया पर्यावरण सहयोग कार्यक्रम, एकीकृत पर्वत विकास के लिए अंतर्रा­ट्रीय केन्द्र की भी प्रमुख एजेंसी है।

भारत वन्य जीव संरक्षण से संबंधित 5 अंतर्रा­ट्रीय समझौतों, वन्य जीव जंतु, वनस्पतियों के संकटापन समूहों के अंतर्रा­ट्रीय व्यापार समझौता, अंतर्रा­ट्रीय व्हेल शिकार आयोग, संयुक्त रा­ट्र शैक्षिक वैज्ञानिक एवं सांस्कृतिक संगठन विश्व विरासत समझौता तथा वन्य पशु प्रवासी समूह संरक्षण समझौता पर हस्ताक्षर करने वाला देश है। इसके तहत मंत्रालय के प्रमुख उद्देश्य वनस्पति जीव जंतु, वन तथा वन्य जीवों का संरक्षण करना है तथा साथ ही प्रदू­ाण की रोकथाम एवं नियंत्रण, विकृत क्षेत्रों में वनरोपण और पुर्नउत्पत्ति, पर्यावरण संरक्षण तथा पशुओं का कल्याण सुनिश्चित करना है।

सरकार ने राज्यों को ऑनलाईन पर्यावरण मंजूरी देने के लिए पहल की है। इसके तहत केन्द्र ने राज्य सरकारों से कहा है कि वह पर्यावरण संबंधी प्रक्रियाओं की ऑनलाईन मंजूरी शुरू करें। इसके लिए परियोजनाओं को राज्यों में स्टेट एनवायरमेंट इम्पेक्ट एसिशसमेंट एथॉरिटी तथा स्टेट एनवायरमेंट एशिसमेंट से मंजूरी हासिल करनी होती है। अभी तक इसके लिए देश में पुरानी प्रक्रिया अपनायी जा रही थी। इस पहल के लिए मैं माननीय मंत्री जी का अभिनन्दन करता हूं।

इसी तरह से सरकार ने देश में विद्युत की कमी को दूर करने के लिए ग्रीन एनर्जी प्रोजेक्ट के लिए 1.71 लाख करोड़ रुपए का ऋण देने का प्रस्ताव किया है, इसके लिए सरकार ने भरोसा दिया है कि इसके माध्यम से सोलर और विंड एनर्जी जैसे गैर-पारम्परिक स्रोतों से 34 हजार मेगावाट विद्युत पैदा की जा सकेगी। इस कार्यक्रम में स्टेट बैंक ऑफ इंडिया ने 75 हजार करोड़ रुपए के कमिटमेंट के साथ अग्रणी रहा है। इससे 15 हजार मेगावाट ग्रीन एनर्जी पैदा की जा सकेगी। इसके बाद 14700 करोड़ रुपए के कमिटमेंट के साथ आईडीबीआई बैंक दूसरे नम्बर पर है। इससे 2940 मेगावाट ग्रीन एनर्जी का उत्पादन हो सकेगा। यह भी ग्रीन एनर्जी उत्पादन की दिशा में सरकार द्वारा उठाया गया एक महत्वपूर्ण कदम है।

भारत सरकार द्वारा पर्यावरण अनुकूल कदम उठाने का ही परिणाम है कि अंतर्रा­ट्रीय ऊर्जा एजेंसी ने भारत द्वारा वैश्विक ताप वृद्धि के लिए प्रमुख रूप से जिम्मेदार गैस कार्बनडाई ऑक्साईड के उत्सर्जन में दुनियाभर में हो रही बढ़ोत्तरी के बावजूद भारत में इसमें कमी आयी है। सरकार ने एक अन्य महत्वपूर्ण पहल करते हुए जलवायु परियोजनाएं लागू करने के लिए देश में एजेंसियों को आमंत्रित किया है जिसके तहत ग्रीन क्लाईमेट फंड के प्रयोग से जलवायु परिवर्तन न्यूनीकरण और उसके अनुकूल परियोजनाओं को लागू करने के लिए पर्यावरण मंत्रालय ने एजेंसियों से आवेदन आमंत्रित किए हैं। जलवायु को­ा से संसाधनों को पाने के लिए आवेदकों को निश्चित तौर पर विश्वासी और मानक प्रबंधन वाला बनाने की दिशा में सरकार द्वारा सार्थक प्रयास किए जा रहे हैं।

आज जब दुनियाभर के तमाम जलवायु वैज्ञानिक चिंतित हैं। जलवायु वैज्ञानिकों का आकंलन है कि अगर बढ़ती हुई ग्लोबल वार्मिंग को नहीं थामा गया तो जल्दी ही दुनिया गरीबी और भूखमरी की चपेट में आ जाएगी। एक अरब से भी ज्यादा लोगों पर इसका सीधा असर होगा, और इसका सबसे ज्यादा असर दक्षिण एशिया पर पड़ेगा। विश्व बैंक ने ग्लोबल वार्मिंग के असर पर अपनी ताजा रिपोर्ट में कहा है कि तापमान बढ़ने से दुनिया के कई इलाकों में फसलों की उत्पादकता में कमी आ रही है। इसमें कोई दो राय नहीं है कि ग्लोबल वार्मिंग के लिए सर्वाधिक दो­ााळ वे देश हैं जो सबसे ज्यादा इसका शोर मचा रहे हैं।

माननीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेन्द्र मोदी जी के नेतृत्व वाली सरकार का यह एक मार्गदर्शक सिद्धांत है कि सरकार समावेशी तरीके से सभी का विकास करेगी। माननीय प्रधानमंत्री जी ने इस बात पर विशे­ा जोर दिया है कि गरीबों के लिए समुचित स्वच्छता, पेयजल, मातृत्व और शिशु देखभाल को सर्वोच्च प्राथमिकता सरकार दें। वैश्विक विकास में भारत की दुनिया में सर्वाधिक महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका है और वैश्विक स्तर पर सहस्त्राब्दि लक्ष्य जब तक सफल नहीं हो सकते तब तक उन्हें भारत में हासिल नहीं किया जाता।

अंत में, मैं पर्यावरण, वन और जलवायु परिवर्तन मंत्रालय द्वारा देश में पर्यावरण के क्षेत्र में किए जा रहे उल्लेखनीय प्रयासों के लिए माननीय प्रधानमंत्री जी एवं माननीय पर्यावरण, वन और जलवायु परिवर्तन मंत्री जी का हार्दिक धन्यवाद करते हुए व­ाऩ 2015-16 की अनुदान मांगों का पुरजोर समर्थन करता हूं।

श्री श्रीरंग आप्पा बारणे (मावल)ः अंतर सरकारी जलवायु परिवर्तन पैनल की व­ाऩ 2014 में प्रकाशित आकलन रिपोर्ट की सिंथेसिस रिपोर्ट में बताया गया है कि सूखे और बाढ़ इत्यादि जैसी जलवायु संबंधी वि­ामताओं से होने वाले प्रभावों में वर्तमान जलवायु से कुछ प्रणालियों और मानव की महत्वपूर्ण रूप से प्रभावित होने का पता चला है। फिर भी, भारत में जलवायु प्रभाव संबंधी कोई विशि­ट अध्ययन उपलब्ध नहीं है, जबकि सरकार का प्रयास है कि प्राकृतिक घटनाओं के वैज्ञानिक आंकलन के आधार पर अनुकूल और उपशमन कार्यों को बढ़ावा दें। सरकार ने 30 जून 2008 को रा­ट्रीय जलवायु परिवर्तन कार्य योजना जारी की थी, जिसमें जलवायु से होने वाली बड़ी घटनाओं की रोकथाम और पूर्व तैयारी के लिए किए जाने वाले उपायों में वृद्धि से जलवायु से होने वाली बड़ी घटना के लिए सभी पहलों को रेखांकित किया जा सके और वर्तमान में सभी राज्य सरकारें भी इसी संबंध में कार्य योजना तैयार कर रही हैं।

जलवायु परिवर्तन, वन और पर्यावरण एक महत्वपूर्ण वि­ाय है, और पूरी दुनिया इस चुनौती से जूझ रही ह।् लेकिन अभी तक इस वि­ाय पर कोई ठोस निर्णय नहीं लिया जा सका है। इसी के चलते, पर्यावरण कानून में बदलाव करने से पहले केन्द्र सरकार राज्यों के साथ व्यापक विचार-विमर्श कर रही है और वर्तमान में पर्यावरण मंजूरी लेना एक बेहद कठिन काम बन गया है,। मंजूरी लेने के लिए लम्बे समय का इंतजार करना पड़ता है, अतः इस प्रक्रिया को ऑनलाइन किए जाने की आवश्यकता है। पर्यावरण से मंजूरी संबंधी परियोजनाओं को राज्यों में स्टेट एनवायरनमेंट अथॉरिटी और स्टेट एनवायरनमेंट असेसमेंट कमेटी से मंजूरी लेनी पड़ती है और अभी तक इसके लिए भी पुरानी प्रक्रिया अपनाई जा रही है। अतः इस प्रक्रिया को बदलकर ऑनलाइन किए जाने की जरूरत है। पर्यावरण को शुद्ध रखने के लिए सभी राज्य नगर पालिकाओं द्वारा उत्पन्न सीवेज को 100 प्रतिशत ट्रीटमेंट करने संबंधी योजना बनायी जानी चाहिए और उद्योग को ट्रीटमेंट के लिए पानी को फिर से इस्तेमाल में लाए जाने पर जोर देना होगा।

पेड़ों के आस-पास कंक्रीट डाले जाने से हरे भरे पेड़ों के सूख जाने का मामला बेहद गंभीर है, और शहरों में इस तरह से हजारों पेड़ सूख गए हैं क्योंकि इन पेड़ों को कंक्रीट से पाट दिया गया है और सरकार द्वारा हरियाली बढ़ाए जाने के खूब दावे किए जाते हैं। इन मामलों में उन मनको का पालन नहीं किया जा रहा है जिनके तहत यह कहा गया है कि पेड़ों की जड़ों के आस-पास एक निर्धारित दूरी तक कंक्रीट नहीं डाला जाना चाहिए, इस तरह से अक्सर देखने को मिलता है कि जैसी ही हवा थोड़ी तेज गति से चलती है या तेज बारिश होती है तो पेड़ गिरने लगते हैं ज्यादातर मामलों में ये पेड़ जड़ो से उखड़ जाते हैं और इस घटना से बड़े पैमाने पर पर्यावरण का नुकसान होता है। इससे जाहिर होता है कि संबंधित एजेंसी को इस ओर विशे­ा ध्यान देने की जरूरत है। सरकार द्वारा वन्य संसाधनों की रक्षा के लिए हरित कानून को सख्ती से लागू किए जाने की जरूरत है, हमारे पास कानून तो बने हैं लेकिन हम उन्हें सख्ती से क्रियान्वित नहीं करते हैं। प्लास्टिक कचरे के प्रबंधन हेतु ठोस कदम उठाए जाने की जरूरत है। देश में धड़ल्ले से नियमों को ताक पर रखकर प्लास्टिक का उपयोग हो रहा है लेकिन हम कोई कार्यवाही नहीं करते हैं। 

दुनिया के तमाम देश इस बात से चिंतित हैं कि अगर ग्लोबल वार्मिंग को यहीं नहीं थामा गया तो जल्द ही दुनिया गरीबी और भुखमरी की चपेट में आ जाएगी और एक अरब से ज्यादा लोगों पर इसका सीधा असर पड़ेगा और सबसे ज्यादा असर दक्षिण एशिया में पड़ेगा। दुनिया भर के वैज्ञानिकों ने इसके प्रति चिंता व्यक्त की है। इसमें कोई दो राय नहीं है कि ग्लोबल वार्मिंग के लिए सर्वाधिक दो­ााळ वो देश हैं जो आज सबसे ज्यादा इसका शोर मचा रहे हैं। यूरोप के विकसित देशों और स्वयं अमेरिका ने पिछली सदी में जबरदस्त औद्योगीकरण करके दुनिया को इस हाल में पहुंचाया है, लेकिन आज ये सब देश मिलकर भारत और चीन को अपनी औद्योगिक नीति बदलने को कह रहे हैं और मोदी जी ने इसी के तहत संयुक्त रा­ट्र महासभा के अपने संबोधन में जलवायु का न केवल जिक्र किया था बल्कि यह भी कहा था कि हम इसकी संवेदनशीलता को भी जानते हैं और ग्लोबल वार्मिंग के चलते दुनिया के कई इलाकों में फसल उत्पादन में कमी हो रही है। यह भवि­य में इस संकट के और गहराने की आशंका है और इसके लिए अगर कोई मजबूत और त्वरित कार्यवाही नहीं की गई तो यह संकट पूरे विश्व में फैल जाएगा।

जलवायु परिवर्तन पर संयुक्त रा­ट्र के मसौद के अनुसार पर्यावरण को होने वाले नुकसान से बचाने के लिए ग्रीन हाउस गैसों के उत्सर्जन कम करने पर सहमति बनी थी लेकिन यह कैसे होगा इस पर पिछले दो दशकों से बिना किसी नतीजे में माथापच्ची जरी है इस काम में सबसे बड़ी बाधा धन की कमी है जिसे पर्यावरण हितै­ााळ प्रौद्योगिकी के विकास पर खर्च किया जाना है। इस पर 2020 तक प्रतिव­ाऩ 100 बिलियन अमेरिकी डॉलर खर्च किया जाना है, इस वि­ाय पर गंभीरता से सोचने की जरूरत है। 

महारा­ट्र में बैल गाड़ी दौड़ प्रतियोगिता का खेल पुराने समय से चलता आ रहा है यह दौड़ महारा­ट्र के हर गाँव में होती है। इस प्रतियोगिता पर किसानों को कोई आपत्ति नहीं थी जबकि इसमें भाग लेने वाले बैलों को किसान अच्छी तरह से पालते हैं और उनकी देखभाल करते हैं यह प्रतियोगिता एक पारंपरिक खेल था पर एनजीओ ने जानवरों पर अत्याचार का मुद्दा उठाकर खेल पर रोक लगाने की मांग की और इस बैलगाड़ी दौड़ प्रतियोगिता पर रोक लगा दी गयी। जहां एक ओर बैलगाड़ी प्रतियोगिता पर रोक लगा दी वहीं दूसरी तरफ घोड़दौड़ अभी भी देश के कई हिस्सों में रेसकोर्स मैदानों में चालू है, मेरा कहना है कि यदि इस बैलगाड़ी दौड़ प्रतियोगिता से जानवरों पर अत्याचार हो रहा है तो इसमें घोड़दौड़ प्रतियोगिता पर रोक क्यों नहीं लगी?अतः मैं सरकार से मांग करता हूं कि महारा­ट्र में पारम्परिक रूप से चली आ रही बैलगाड़ी दौड़ प्रतियागिता पर रोक को यथापूर्व हटाए जाने हेतु आवश्यक कदम उठाए जाने की कार्यवाही सरकार द्वारा की जाए।

इको सेंसेटिव जोन देश के कई भागों में हैं जो कि निश्चित रूप से पर्यावरण के रख-रखाव के लिए बनाए गए हैं। लेकिन वर्तमान समय में इन इको सेंसेटिव जोन से इन क्षेत्रों में जाने वाले नागरिकों एवं पर्यटकों को बहुत सी कठिनाई का सामना करना पड़ता है। मेरे संसदीय क्षेत्र में प्रसिद्ध पर्यटन क्षेत्र माथेरान है। यह क्षेत्र ब्रिटिश काल से ही इको सेंसेटिव जोन घो­िात कया गया है और इको सेंसेटिव जोन घो­िात होने की वजह से यहां पर डीजल गाड़ियों एवं अन्य वाहनों के चलने पर रोक लगी हुई है। माथेरान 25 हजार का आबादी वाला क्षेत्र है। यहाँ के बच्चों को कई किलोमीटर पैदल चलकर स्कूल जाना पड़ता है। यहाँ इन सब वाहनों के नहीं होने से स्थानीय लोगों को अनेक कठिनाइयों का सामना करना पड़ता है। सेंसेटिव जोन होने के कारण यहां के लोग अपने मकानों की मरम्मत नहीं कर सकते हैं। यहां आवा- गमन के लिए कोई भी सुविधा नहीं होने के कारण यहां पर्यटकों को ले जाने के लिए हाथगाड़ी का उपयोग होता है। जो नवजवान रोजी रोटी के लिए हाथ गाड़ी खींचने का काम करते हैं वह अपनी थकान को दूर करने के लिए नशा करते हैं।

अतः मैं सरकार से मांग करता हूं कि माथेरान जैसे हिल स्टेशन में बैटरी से चलाए जाने वाले रिक्शा शुरू करने की अनुमति दी जाए और पर्यटकों को आकर्­िात करने हेतु वहां रोप वे की सुविधा दी जाए जिससे नवजवानों को रोजगार मिलेगा और केन्द्र और राज्य सरकार से मैं इसके लिए आर्थिक मदद की मांग करता हूं। 

SHRI RAM PRASAD SARMAH (TEZPUR): I come from Tezpur Constituency of Assam. I fully support the Demand for Grants to the Ministry of Environment and Forests.

Assam, once used to be known as “Forest State” with richest bounty of forests and wild life and different types of flora and medical plants. But during the last 15 years of Congress rule in the State there has been systematic denodation of forest and killing of wild life. The world famous one-horn rhino is facing serious threat from poachers, as many as 79 rhinos have been killed in only last three years. Sand mining and illegal quarrying of valuable forest mines and minerals have been going on unabated and the State Government is a mute spectator. Smuggling of rhino horn, tiger skin, keko reptile and other wild life parts is indiscriminately going on in Assam, Kaziranga, Manas, Pobitara and Orang known for one horn rhino serious threat due to encouraged encroachment.

Tribal communities living in forest villages in forest areas are not given the rights by the State Government, as is required under the Forest Rights Act, 2006.

Therefore, I would request the Ministry to take strong steps to check forest demarcation, killing of rhinos and smuggling of animal parts and also stop illegal mining and smuggling of sand and other valuable minerals in the State. I also request the hon’ble Minister to embark on large scale plantation of trees in the areas where forest cover has been reduced due to illegal felling of tree.

The NHAI has not yet planted trees filled during 4 laning of roads in Assam. 

The Environment & Forest Ministry should direct the NHAI to plant road vide trees on the stretch of 4 laning road. I may add that about 3 lakh valuable and fully grown up tree were felled by NHAI during lane conversion. 

*SHRI TATHAGATA SATPATHY (DHENKANAL): We, as a nation, have long ignored climate change and its effects on our environment in the name of 'development', but it's time to reconsider our objectives and goals so that they are more in sync with our biodiversity. After 100 days of the new government, a four-member high-level committee headed by former Cabinet Secretary T.S.R. Subramanian was formed to examine five laws; The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980, the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, and the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981. The order says that the committee would 'recommend specific amendments needed in each of these acts to bring them in line with current requirements to meet objectives.' That does not sound very encouraging . Due to the launch of the single-window environment and forest clearance system, it is highly doubtful if the government will swing in favour of environment protection and preservation. 

I will concentrate my speech broadly on two things; rampant use of non-biodegradable material (namely, plastic) and effects of climate change.

Plastic was produced for the first time in 1856, during the industrial revolution. It was hailed as a major advance in the world industry. Today, we find plastics everywhere, pet bottles that contain beverages, polyester, kitchen utensils, packaging material, electronics and much more.

According to an industry summary by Indian Brand Equity Foundation (IBEF), currently, the Indian plastics industry is spread across the country, employing about 4 million people and over 2,000 exporters. It operates more than 30,000 processing units, of which 85 per cent to 90 per cent are small and medium enterprises (SMEs).

The President of All India Plastic Manufacturer's Association (AIPMA) has stated that the per capita consumption of plastic is 9.7 kg per person in India, while the global average is 27 kg. We are still far away from the global average but the consumption is steadily increasing. As the standard of living of people goes up, they start consuming more FMCG products which use plastics for packaging their products quite liberally. 

This is a worrying trend because once plastic is created, it cannot be destroyed. 'Recycle plastics' is the new motto of the Plastic industry. Industry leaders has even gone so far as to say that plastic bags are 'environment friendly' in a statement issued by AIPMA on 8 February 2015. I would like to ask them whether there is any way to destroy unused plastic in an environment friendly manner? 

Let me put forward a worrying scenario which is unfolding right now far in the Pacific ocean. National Geographic recently reported a story about 'The Great Pacific Garbage Patch' which proves to be quite an eye-opener. The Great Pacific Garbage Patch, also known as the Pacific trash vortex, spans waters from the West Coast of North America to Japan. It is full of non-biodegradable garbage which is stuck in a vortex, in the middle of the ocean. The garbage patch is estimated to be as big as the state of Texas.

The report says, 'A plastic water bottle discarded off the coast of California takes the California Current south toward Mexico. There, it may catch the North Equatorial Current, which acrosses the vast Pacific. Near the coast of Japan, the bottle may travel north on the powerful Kuroshiro Current. Finally, the bottle travels westward on the North Pacific Current. The gently rolling vortexes of the Eastern and Western Garbage Patches gradually draw in the bottle.'

The amount of debris in the Great Pacific Garbage Patch accumulates because much of it is not biodegradable. Many plastics do not wear down; they simply break into tinier and tinier pieces. These 'microplastics' are then ingested by sea creatures and get stuck in plants under the ocean. This is turn goes further up the food-chain and ends up in restaurants that serve sea food. Since these are micro-plastics, they are difficult to see with the naked eye. These are getting ingested by humans too.

Nobody knows exactly how much plastic is stuck in that humongous vortex, since it's really difficult to estimate the quantity. Scientists have collected up to 750,000 bits of microplastic in a single square kilometer of the Great Pacific Garbage Patch- that's about 1.9 million bits per square mile. Most of this debris comes from plastic bags, bottle caps, plastic water bottles, and Styrofoam cups. About 80% of the debris in the Great Pacific Garbage Patch comes from land-based activities in North America and Asia. Trash from the coast of North America takes about six years to reach the Great Pacific Garbage Patch, while trash from Japan and other Asian countries takes about a year.

Instances like these should immediately ring some alarm bells. The recent Kashmir and Uttarakhand floods are examples of what happens if we are flippant about protecting our environment and forests. Even after those floods, the lessen seems to be lost on us. The state government there has cleared 26 projects which will cause massive deforestation. The Central Government has given a green signal for removing the requirement of forest clearances around border areas, stating national security and defence. 

Climate Change is a slow process. It is not immediately recognizable but the effects are all around us. The change in the behaviour of monsoons and the resulting crop damage being the biggest one of them. April 22 was celebrated as Earth Day throughout the world. On that day, a group of US scientists opined that a quarter of the total fossil fuel available on earth needs to remain inside the earth. Scientists warn us that climate change would accelerate beyond our control, threatening our survival and everything we love. We need to act fast to keep global temperature rise under the unacceptable dangerous level of 2 degrees C, by phasing out carbon pollution to zero. To achieve this, we must urgently forge realistic global, national and local agreements, to rapidly shift our societies and economies to 100% clean energy by 2050.

During a student interaction at Assam last year, our Prime Minister said: 'Climate change? Is this terminology correct? The reality is this that in our family some people are old. They say this time the weather is colder. And, people's ability to bear cold becomes less. We should also ask is this climate change or have we changed. We have battled against nature. That is why we should live with nature rather than battle it. ' In a United Nations conference on climate change, mere days after making this comment, Mr. Modi was a no show. Thoughts translate into action. It would be unsurprising if the Damodardass government goes on to include these untruths in curriculum across the country. This is a very real fear. 

You see reports about torrential flooding and other extreme weather on the news pretty much all of the time- some may argue, but it looks like climate change caused by human activity is indeed a real thing. Polar icebergs melting at increasingly alarming rates will cause sea levels to rise in the future. On the flip side of the coin, the fire season in the hot, dry regions of the west coast of North America lasts roughly 75 days longer than it did a decade ago. 

The world of climate governance is in a flux. A series of extreme weather events, from India to Australia, to the Philippines, continues to periodically ring alarm bells on climate change. The rolling release of the inter-governmental Panel on Climate Change's Fifth Assessment report provides ever more sober calls for the need for action. 

Yet, in most countries, and in global dialogue, levels of political attention to climate change are declining, crowded out by the financial crisis and other short term crises. At the same time, more countries than ever before- covering an estimated 67% of global emissions - have in place some form of national legislation or strategy to address climate change. There has also been a proliferation of informal local initiatives and transnational networks. 

The United Nations Climate Change Conference, COP21 or CMP11 will be held in Paris, France in November 2015. It is expected to be one of the biggest climate change conferences in the world, where 196 countries will meet to sign agreements regarding reduction of carbon emissions. This is a historic opportunity for India to show that we are serious about climate change and willing to take a stand. We are being increasingly seen as a pro-industry and anti-environment nation. Especially after this government decided to rapidly give environmental clearances on one hand and ban organizations like Greenpeace on the other, we are not seeing welcome signs which say otherwise. I urge the government to make a proper plan before going to this conference and share it with the House. There needs to be proper consultations regarding this mater and we must take a united stand against climate change. 

*KUMARI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE (UDUPI CHIKMAGALUR): The concept of Ecologically Sensitive Areas (ESAs) in the Western Ghats has been a contentious issue from the start. Dr. K. Kasturirangan Committee Report earmarked 59,940 sq. km (37%) of the Western Ghats as ESAs. The MoEF outlines a draft Notification based on this Report on March 10,2014, identifying a total of 56,825 sq. km in six states that straddle the Western Ghats. Karnataka represents the biggest chunk of the ESAs. The proposal to declare 20,668 sq. km of Karnataka's Western Ghats as ESAs has raised fears of relocation among local communities, although the report only recommends banning activities such as mining and thermal plants in these areas.

Kasturirangan Committee Report has faced opposition from various quarters including environmentalists and people living in and around the Western Ghats belt. People living in the vicinity were in the grip of fear that the implementation of the Report would adversely affect their livelihood. Government of Karnataka had requested the Union Government to keep habitations, plantations and agricultural areas in villages out of the purview of the ESAs. Of karnataka's total geographical area of 1,91,791 sq. km Western Ghats taluks measure up to 44,448 sq. km, including 1,576 villages identified as ESAs. I suggest that the Government should adopt a more liberal approach while dealing with this sensitive issue. Recently, Karnataka Government has sought extension of time to give its comments on the K. Kasturirangan Report on conservation of Western Ghats to the Centre. So far, only Kerala has submitted its objections to the Centre.

The magnanimity of pollution has been slowly, but certainly acquiring serious proportions. Protection of environment has not been accorded due priority by the state governments, particularly in view of fact that without their support and cooperation, it would not be possible for the Government alone to ensure environmental protection. It may not be practically feasible for the Government alone to fight and tackle the menace of rapid rise in pollution witnessed all over- air, water, land, noise, etc. throughout the length and breadth of the country. Necessary cooperation and support from the state governments is definitely required in this regard. Government will always find it difficult to control the rapid pace at which the health of environment and conditions of natural resources is deteriorating day by day unless and until the state governments are made effective partners in protection of the environment. 

One disturbing news appearing in the media is that air pollution was the 5th biggest killer in India, other reports related to hazardous smog like situation in the making in the Indian cities due to excessive air pollution. As per the report appearing in the media, close to half of cities are reeling under severe particular pollution while newer pollutants like Nitrogen Oxide, Ozone and air toxins are worsening public health challenge. 

As per the Annual Report 2012-2013 of the Ministry, 131 cities exceed the permissible limit of PM10 which is as high as 62 per cent and 19 cities exceed the level of NO2. Continuous growth of municipal solid waste generation in urban areas of the country has also emerged as one of the biggest polluters of environment. According to a recent Survey of Central Pollution Control Board CPCB) in 60 major cities of the country, the total municipal solid waste generated is 50,592 tons per day, while the country wide generation is estimated to be of the volume of 1,50,000 tons per day. Out of the above, only a small portion is being processed and the remaining waste is dumped in an open air leading to environmental and health hazards in cities and towns. As per CPCB assessment, India generates 56 lakhs tonnes of plastic waste annually. Out of the total plastic waste generation in the country only approximately 60% is collected and recycled, while the rest remain uncollected and littered.

I suggest that the Ministry should conduct a Study of its own, on mortality due to air pollution in major Indian cities and in case the Study confirms the findings of the Report published by the Centre for Science and Education (CSE), take urgent remedial measures to prevent the adverse impacts of air pollution on health of citizens.

I wish to express my serious concerns over the rapid rise in all types of pollution and feel that unless some serious and effective steps are taken by the CPCB, the situation would continue to go from bad to worse; assume alarming proportions in days to come and prove to be detrimental for the entire country. Adequate expansion and strengthening of monitoring and enforcing agencies is the need of the hour so that the situation does not deteriorate further. Efforts should also be made to further increase the number of Zonal Offices of CPCB so that effective and successful monitoring of projects/polluting units could be undertaken. 

I appreciate the measures taken by the Ministry to streamline the environment and forestry clearances which would facilitate speedy execution of large developmental projects. Smaller projects involving requirement of forestry clearance for some 5 kms. or 10 kms roads, building hospitals have been hanging fire since long. I feel that there is a need to adopt positive approach to give clearance to projects which are badly required for development. 

Public hearing has been made mandatory in the schemes of things of according Environmental Clearance/Forest Clearance for some of the projects particuarly those which affect the local inhabitants, the fact is that public hearing is not conducted in an objective and impartial manner. Often public hearing becomes a state managed and an eye-wash show conducted in the presence of the project proponents where their representatives use it as a platform to persuade, convince and coax the affected public to give their nod for the project to the detriment of their interest and welfare. Such instances give rise to discontentment among the public and sometimes also result in protest putting the entire project in jeopardy. Government must take necessary measures to curb such malpractices in public hearing so that public hearing serves the purpose for which these are intended. Genuine concerns of the people must find place in the environment management plan and project proponents take necessary preventive and curative measures to address the genuine concerns of the public. I suggest that the Ministry should take up monitoring in a few sample cases of actual implementation of various safeguards for public hearing laid in EIA Notification so as to find out as to what extent the provision of EIA Notifications are being adhered to in actual practice. 

There is an urgent need to save the species facing extinction and reduce significantly, if not eliminate altogether, incidents that kill animals like man-animal conflict, rail or road accidents etc. the Ministry must takes all necessary measures, local inhabitants should be involved in a big way for providing protection to the wild animals, as well as, to forest cover. The incidents like man-animal conflict, death of elephants due to rail accidents, etc. continue unabated, the Ministry should conduct a comparative study so as to know as to what extent the measures taken have helped reduce killing of animals. 

SHRI NAGENDRA KUMAR PRADHAN (SAMBALPUR): Sir, these Demands for Grants consist of three parts – the first one deals with forests, another with environment and the third one deals with climate change. 

Let me begin with environment. Now, inklings of some of the projections have started manifesting in India in the form of devastating natural calamities, flash floods in Uttarakhand, back to back floods in Kashmir, severe cyclonic storms like Phailin and Hudhud. They are some of the recent instances. The cycle of monsoon has gone erratic affecting paddy cultivation in large parts of the country. The natural flow of major rivers including the Ganga, Yamuna, Mahanadi, Brahmani in Odisha are showing a declining trend. The condition of lakes, rivers and other water bodies continues to deteriorate day by day despite efforts made by the Government. Worsening air quality in the country in general and in Delhi in particular has been making headlines earning ignominy at the national andinternatinal levels so much so that some of the countries have reportedly reduced the tenure of their diplomats in Delhi and many Embassies have installed air purifiers in their offices and residences of their diplomats. 

A study ‘Lower Pollution, Longer Lives’ published in the Economic and Political Weekly on 21st February 2015 has estimated that India can save up to two billion life years and about 3.2 years per person if 660 million people living in areas exceeding the National Ambient Air Quality for PM 2.5 pollution can breathe air which meets air quality standards. This should be a clarion call to proactively and effectively act in a time bound manner before it is too late because environmental damage beyond a certain level becomes irreparable and irreversible. It is most unfortunate that in a recent response filed in the High Court of Delhi, the Government has stated that there is no Action Plan so far to address the critical challenges of air pollution in the Capital. So, I want a clarification on this point. Not only metropolitan cities but even Tier-II, smaller towns and cities are found to be reeling under the severe impact of pollution on all environmental parameters. 

The State is constitutionally mandated to protect and improve the environment and safeguard our forests and wildlife. The Constitution recognises the duty of every citizen of India to protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife. The principle of sustainable development is incorporated as an integral component of the Right to Life under Article 21 of the Constitution. Despite all this, the challenges of environmental degradation remain unaddressed. 

The environmental degradation which is considered to be a major contributing factor in loss of agricultural productivity, because ecological degradation affects soil fertility, quantity and quality of water, air quality, forests, wildlife and fisheries etc. The worst sufferers of forest degradation are the poor tribal societies who live on natural resources. The loss of environmental resource base often results in these groups being made destitute which leads to alienation and exhaustion of large segment of our population. 

Coal-based thermal power plants are one of the most polluting ways of producing power in the world. In India, about 70 per cent of the power is provided by coal. The high dependence on coal, however, comes at a significant cost to the environment. Not only do coal-based thermal power plants result in large scale emission of particulate matter and other pollutants such as SO2, NOx and mercury but they also produce 170 million odd tonnes of poorly managed fly ash and consume tremendous quantities of water in the course of their operations. I want to draw the attention of the hon. Minister through you whether he is thinking of any alternative like renewable energy and so on. I would like him to provide some information on this. 

Now I come to the second part, that is, Forestry. The National Forest Policy, 1988 envisages the national goal of having minimum of 33 per cent of the total land area of the country under forests or tree cover. The break-up of the forest and tree cover as per India -- State of Forest Report, 2013 shows that the total forest and tree cover of 24.01 per cent comprises of 2.54 per cent of very dense forest, 9.70 per cent of moderate dense forest, 8.99 per cent of open forest and 2.78 per cent of tree cover. The percentage of very dense forest continues to be at 2.54 ever since the year 2007. Thus, the forest cover in true sense of the term as per the 2013 Report constitutes only 12.2 per cent of the total geographical area of the country. 

National Afforestation Programme was launched in 2002-03 to improve forest cover and livelihood of the people living in and around forest areas for which an outlay of Rs.2,500 crore was approved for the Twelfth Five-Year Plan. Out of that, an amount of Rs.663.45 crore, approximately 1/4th of the total approved outlay, was spent during the last three years. This year the allocation has been reduced from Rs.243.8 crore at the BE level in 2014-15 to Rs.100 crore. In all likelihood, the entire outlay earmarked for National Afforestation Programme for the Twelfth Five-Year Plan is not going to be fully utilised.

The funding pattern of the National Afforestation Programme is likely to undergo a change with the share of Centre and States at 50:50 from 2015-16 onwards instead of existing 100 per cent Central share. This change in funding pattern would definitely affect the progress of the programme as the States, owing to their own priorities, may not like to contribute to this programme as expected by the Ministry. Therefore, my humble request to you is that the earlier condition of 100 per cent funding by Government of India should continue to exist. 

Of the total BE allocation of Rs.80 crore for 2014-15, only Rs.3 crore could be utilised. Yet, this year outlay for this scheme has been kept at Rs.64 crore. The hon. Minister should explain during his reply as to how this money would be spent. 

Is it a fact that an amount to the tune of Rs.38,000 crore is lying with in Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA)? As per the directions of the Supreme Court, the Ministry is supposed to release the funds only to the extent of ten per cent of the principal amount of about Rs.23,800 and that also from the interest accrued. This year although the Ministry was authorised to release about Rs.2,400 crore, it could release only Rs.1,100 crore. In this connection, what is the position of this CAMPA fund?

In reply to a question the hon. Minister for Environment, Forests and Climate Change stated that one lakh hectares of forest land had been diverted for mining projects in Chhattisgarh State which is the largest patch of land. Other States must be doing things that way. Thank you.

Environmentalists in India have expressed their anguish and alarm over this cut in the allocation and they fear that it would affect more environmental programmes in the country, which would result in the failure to address the worsening pollution and vulnerability to climate change. So, I humbly request our Hon. Finance Minister to allocate more funds, as in it western countries, for more research programmes on pollution, climate change, renewable energy and solar for rural use.

Yet another worrying and shocking matter in the Budget is that the funding to the National Mission on Sustainable Agriculture has been reduced by 80 per cent this year, from 15 billion rupees to 3 billion rupees. Agriculture is our primary source of greenhouse gas emission in India because of paddy cultivation, which produces methane through extended flooding fields and the use of cows to farm small plots of land.

Farming is also highly at risk from climate change impacts, particularly changing rainfall patterns, floods, drought and storms. I hail from the Cauvery Delta region where agriculture is main source of living of more 80 per cent of population. 

I request our Hon. Finance Minister to allocate more funds to the Ministry of Environment and also allocate sufficient funds for states to implement programmes on pollution, climate change and sustainable agriculture, renewable energy, solar for rural use etc.

I request our Hon. Minister that Bio-diversity is one of the important aspects we have to consider seriously because among the 25 Hotspots present globally, India plays vital role in the presence of varieties of fauna and flora. Gangetic plains, Gulf of Mannar Reserves, mangrove forests and western Ghats are the diversified ecosystem in India. Migratory birds which come even from Syberia to our country should be monitored carefully. Environmental pollution, poaching, destruction of habitat are the reason for bio-diversity loss.

The Vaduvur birds sanctuary is under my constituency. It should be protected to maintain the migratory birds visit from various places. If the Ministry of Environment and Forest take initiative, vaduvur bird's sanctuary will become in future as one of the important tourist attractive place as like Kodiakkaraji, Vedanthangail and Udhayamarthandapuram in Tamil Nadu.

Hence, I request the Hon. Minister for Environment and Forest to take necessary action to make the Vaduvur bird's sanctuary as one of the important Research centre as like Dr. Salim Ali's Ornithological Research Centre. It paves the way to create awareness among the public about birds bio-diversity and also to produce more number of young scientists in our country.

The Kodhandaramar Temple with beautiful Ramar idol locate in the banks of Vaduvur birds sanctuary attract thousands of pilgrims from various parts of our country. If the Tourism Ministry establishes Boat club in Vaduvur lake it will also provides facilities to the school children, pilgrims, tourist, environmentalist and general public which in turn would generate revenue to the government.

Finally, I request our Hon. Finance Minister to allocate more funds to the Ministry of Environment, allocate sufficient funds for states to implement the research centre in Vaduvur, Tamil Nadu and to develop Vaduvur Birds Sanctuary. 

*SHRI ADHALRAO PATIL SHIVAJIRAO (SHIRUR): I am thankful for giving me an opportunity to express my views on this important issue. I am sure, with the help of the balanced budget presented by the Government, the Ministry of Environment and Forests will function more efficiently and smoothly. I wish to draw kind attention of the Government towards two important issues pertaining to violation of Forest Act, 2006 with the help of Lokshashan Andolan and banning of bulls to participate in the ritual functions in the State of Maharastra.

Forest is a unique natural component of environment system. Aforestation is necessary for enrichment of forest but more important is protection of existing forest. Forest has to be protected from illicit felling of trees, encroachment, grazing, hunting and fire. Existing forest area is first to be protected from encroachment and then forest area is to be enriched by planting of seedlings. Even at places merely protection encourages natural regeneration. Increased population, industrialization and decreased forest produce are major reasons for forest degradation. Illegal encroachment on forest land should not be encouraged or regularized. Indirectly, it supports forest offences and demoralizes forest department. The forest were declared as reserved forest by following due procedure in which rights, privileges of peoples in forest have been enquired and settled.

The scheduled Tribes and other Traditional forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 and Rules 2008 is an Act to recognize vesting of the forest rights and occupation in forest land in for forest dwelling scheduled tribes and other traditional forest dwellers who have been residing in such forests for generations but whose right could not be recorded, to provide for a frame work for recording the forest rights so vested of the nature of evidence required for such recognition of vesting in respect of forest land. In this Act 'forest dwelling scheduled tribes' means the members of community of the Scheduled Tribes who primarily reside in and who depend on forests lands for bona-fide livelihood needs and includes the Scheduled Tribe pastoralist communities. 

Similarly, 'other traditional forest dwellers' means any member or community, who has for at least three generations prior to the 13th day of December, 2005 primarily resided in and who depend on the forest or forests land for bona fide livelihood needs.'

This Act gives only right over the forest land to Scheduled tribes and other traditional forest dwellers. Scheduled procedure has been laid down for giving these rights to them. This procedure mainly includes formation of village level, sub division level and district level committees and claims under this Act will be settled and decided at these committee level only. The deadline for giving legal entitlement was 13th December, 2005.

However, in part of Western Maharahstra particularly around Pune district Lokshashan Andolan is headed by Shri B.G. Kolse Patil and Shri P.B. Sawant, Preisent of Lokshashan Andolan. In this andolan, the so called activists are encroaching on forest land and claiming their rights which is illegal. These activists are creating law and order problem by coming in a mob including ladies, small children and old-aged persons so that even the Forest Department is not in a position to evict the mob and these mobs encroach precious forest land. Even the local leaders and people support them in connivance with the forest officials. It is a high time to reconsider the policy while implementing the spirit of the Act and to stop encroachment on forest land by unauthorized activists/people encroaching upon the forest land in connivance with the forest officials unauthorized by mis-interpreting the law. I urge to issue necessary directions to all the State Governments to register cases against these encroachers and to implement the law in its letter and spirit strictly so that only those people who are eligible can be benefited. 

One more important issue towards which I wish to draw the kind attention is pertaining to inclusion of Bulls in the Notification dated 11th July, 2011, as wild animal published in the Gazette of India, issued by the Ministry of Environment and Forests. With the effect of Gazette, the training and performance of Bull is prohibited. As you are aware, there is a long practice since our ancestral days for performing a religious programme once in a year which also includes Bull for Bullock Cart Race in Maharahstra and Jallikattu in Tamil Nadu. However, special care has been taken during the occasion that the Bulls are not harmed during the religious programmes so conducted. These programmes were being taken at different places in Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. However, after publication of the above Notification in the Gazette of India, participation of Bulls has been restricted and Bulls are not allowed to participate in the function by the local administration. This has hurt the sentiments of the local people.

Keeping in view the religious function involving Bulls fairs are being being performed since last hundreds of years from our ancestral days and also keeping in view the fact that the bulls are not harmed in any manner during the religious function, the name of the Bull may be excluded from the list of animals by bringing out necessary amendment to Section 22 of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 (59 of 1960) and accordingly the Notification dated 11th July, 2011may be amended to that extent. 

श्री रत्न लाल कटारिया (अम्बाला)ः मैं बजट में पर्यावरण, वन एवं क्लाइमेट चेंज मंत्रालय संबंधी अनुदान मांगों का समर्थन करता हूं। मुझे इस बात की खुशी है कि प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेन्द्र मोदी जी के नेतृत्व में हमारे देश में 5871 सक्वेयर किमी एरिया वनों की दृ­िट से बड़ा है। यह बात अलग है कि कई राज्यों में यह बढ़ा है और कई राज्यों में घटा है जैसा कि नॉर्थ ईस्ट में वनों का एरिया जो पहले 75 प्रतिशत से भी अधिक होता था वह 627 सक्वेयर किमी घटा है। भारत सरकार वनों के अन्धा-धुंध कटाव को लेकर अति गम्भीर है। इसी प्रकार से, भारत सरकार पर्यावरण व क्लाइमेट चेंज के मुद्दे पर भी गंभीर है। 

हाल ही में जेनेवा में क्लाइमेट चेंज को लेकर जो सम्मेलन हुआ था उसमें भारत ने जोरदार ढंग से यह आवाज उठाई थी कि विकसित देशों को पर्यावरण से हो रही हानि की भरपाई करनी चाहिए और इसके लिए विकसित देशों ने यह संकल्प भी लिया था कि वे ग्रीन क्लाइमेट फंड में 10 बिलियन राशि प्रदान करेंगे। इनमें यूएस, जापान, यूके, जमनी, फ्रांस व स्वीडन जैसे देश शामिल थे परन्तु बड़े दुख की बात है कि इन देशों ने केवल मात्र 1.03 प्रतिशत ही ग्रीन क्लाइमेट फंड के लिए अपना वायदा पूरा किया। भारत ने इस बात को भी बड़े जोरदार ढंग से उठाया है। अभी 2015 में जो क्लाइमेट चेंज को लेकर पेरिस में विश्व सम्मेलन होने जा रहा है, भारत उसमें भी जोरदार ढंग से अपनी बात रखेगा। भारत ने प्रदू­ाण को कम करने की दृ­िट से अपने देश की सभी नदियों को पर्यावरण से बचाने के लिए व्यापक कदम उठाए हैं जैसा कि- गंगा की सफाई के लिए व्यापक अभियान छेड़ा गया है, जिसके लिए बजट में 2000 करोड़ रुपए का प्रावधान भी रखा गया है। परन्तु इस दिशा में अभी और ठोस कदम उठाने होंगे। क्योंकि आज भी बड़े-बड़े शहरों का 90 से 95 प्रतिशत तक सिवरेज का गंदा पानी इन नदियों में गिर रहा है। यूएनओ की एक रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक भारत के बड़े-बड़े 20 शहर दुनिया के सबसे प्रदू­िात शहर हैं जिनमें आज जीना दूभर हो गया है। आज हमारे देश की राजधानी को ही ले लो, आज यहां पर इतना कार्बन या इतना प्रदू­ाण है कि सांस लेना भी मुश्किल है। अगर हमने इस दिशा में कोई ठोस कदम न उठाए तो देश को इसकी भारी कीमत चुकानी पड़ सकती है। आज प्रदू­ाण हमारे देश के स्वास्थ्य के लिए खतरनाक स्तर पर पहुंच गया है। अगर हमने डीजल वाहनों से पैदा होने वाले प्रदू­ाण पर रोक न लगाई और नई टैक्नोलॉजी का इस्तेमाल करके अपनी रिफाइनरीज में सुधार नहीं किया, तो हम क्लीन एनर्जी लेने में विफल रहेंगे। इसी प्रकार से, हमारे देश में कचरा मैनेजमेंट की भी एक बहुत बड़ी समस्या है और अब तो इस सोलिड वेस्ट के साथ-साथ हमारा देश ई-वेस्ट दुनिया के 5वें नम्बर पर पैदा करने लगा है। मैं बधाई देना चाहूंगा कि सरकार ने कोयले पर यू.टी 100 प्रतिशत से बढ़ाकर 200 प्रतिशत प्रतिटन की है। परन्तु इससे मिलने वाली राशि को हमें अपने प्रदू­ाण को कम करने पर ही खर्च करना होगा। 

अभी-अभी यूएनओ की एक रिपोर्ट आई है कि भारत को अपने देश में आने वाली आपदाओं से दस बिलियन डॉलर प्रतिव­ाऩ हानि उठानी पड़ रही है। भारत में भूकम्प से 19 मिलियन डॉलर, साइक्लोन से 447 मिलियन डॉलर, तूफानों से 727 मिलियन डॉलर, सूनामी से 1160 , बाढ़ से 4772 मिलियन डॉलर यानि की कुल मिलाकर 10 बिलियन डॉलर के लगभग प्रतिव­ाऩ हानि उठानी पड़ रही है। मोदी सरकार ने इस दिशा में ध्यान दिया है और भारत ने क्लाइमेट चेंज को लेकर हो रहे विश्व सम्मेलनों में भारत की इस प्रतिबद्धता को जताया है कि वह आने वाले 5 व­ााॉ में 9 बिलियन डॉलर अपने आपदा प्रबंधन पर खर्च करेगा। यूएनओ रिपोर्टस में इस बात का भी खुलासा किया गया है कि इगर हम आपदा प्रबंधन पर 6 बिलियन डॉलर खर्च करते हैं तो हम आपदाओं के मामले में 360 बिलियन का फायदा उठा सकते हैं। इससे हमारी आपदाओं में 20 प्रतिशत की कमी होगी। मैं यह कहना चाहता हूं कि आज हमारे देश के 4.8 मिलियन भारतीय पर्यावरण के कारण होने वाली आपदाओं से पीड़ित हैं। अगर हमने युद्धस्तर पर इस दिशा में कदम न उठाए तो 2030 तक भारत के 19 मिलियन लोग प्रभावित हो सकते हैं। 

आज नेपाल में क्लाइमेट चेंज के कारण एक भयंकर आपदा आई है। मैं बधाई देना चाहता हूं, अपने प्रधानमंत्री को, जिन्होंने प्रंट पर आकर इस मामले में लीड किया है और नेपाल के पीड़ित लोगों को राहत पहुंचाई है। उन्होंने आज भी अपने कई केन्द्रीय मंत्रियों को बिहार, पश्चिम बंगाल व उत्तर प्रदेश के साथ लगे इलाकों में पीड़ितों को राहत पहुंचाने में पहल की है।

हमारे देश की 50 करोड़ जनता हिमालय रीजन के क्षेत्र में रहती है। अगर हमने क्लाइमेट चेंज की ओर युद्धस्तर पर ध्यान नहीं दिया तो जिस प्रकार से, हमालय की तलहटी में चेंजिज आ रही हैं जिसके कारण हमारे ग्लेशियर पिघल रहे हैं और उसके परिणामस्वरूप हमारी नदियों में उफान आ रहा है। अगर हम समय पर नहीं चेते तो तटों पर रहने वाले हमारे शहरों के लिए बड़ा खतरा पैदा हो जाएगा। संयुक्त रा­ट्र संघ ने यह भी चेतावनी दी है कि 21वीं सदी के अन्त तक दुनिया के ग्लेशियर ग्लोबल वार्मिंग के कारण इतना पिघल सकते हैं कि समुद्र तल का स्तर 85 सेंटीमीटर तक बढ़ जाए जिसके कारण दुनिया के समुद्र के किनारे पर रहने वाले बड़े-बड़े नगरों को भी खतरा पैदा हो सकता है। हमारे देश में भी जिस प्रकार से तमिलनाडु के अंदर कई बार सूनामी आई है। यह सब हमारे देश में जो कार्बन उत्सर्जन हो रहा है, यह एक मुख्य कारण है। आज हमें अपने देश में एयर क्वालिटी की मॉनिटरिंग के लिए संस्थागत ढांचा खड़ा करने की जरूरत है। मैं तो चाहूंगा कि जो वाहन ज्यादा प्रदू­ाण पैदा रकते हैं उनके प्रदू­ाण कंट्रोल के लिए नई-नई टैक्नालॉजी का इस्तेमाल करना चाहिए और यहां तक कि ऐसे वाहनों पर टैक्स भी लगाया जाना चाहिए। मैं चाहूंगा कि सरकार अब पब्लिक ट्रांसपोर्ट प्रदान कराने की दिशा में भी कदम उठाए ताकि बड़े-बड़े शहरों में सांस लेना आसान हो सके।

मुझे बड़ी खुशी है कि भारत सरकार वनों को बढ़ावा देने के लिए ठोस कदम उठा रही है क्योंकि अन्धा-धुंध वनों के कटान से ग्लोबल वार्मिंग को बढ़ावा मिल रहा है। हालात यहाँ तक पहुंच गए -

"अब तो थक गए पंख भी उड़ती चिड़िया के,

क्योंकि एक वृक्ष से दूसरे वृक्ष की दूरी इतनी तो बढ़ गई "

हमने अपनी प्रकृति का विनाश इस ढंग से किया है कि अब घरों में न कहीं चिड़िया चहकती हुई नजर आती है और न ही कहीं बईयों के धौंसलें नजर आते है।

अन्त में, मैं उन सभी मदों का समर्थन करता हूं जिन मदों के अंतर्गत पर्यावरण वन और जलवायु मंत्रालयों के लिए अनुदानों का प्रावधान किया गया है। मुझे पूरी उम्मीद है कि भारत सरकार भारत की 125 करोड़ की जनता को प्रदू­ाणमुक्त करने एवं खुली हवा में सांस दिलाने के लिए कोई कसर बाकी नहीं छोड़ेगी।

SHRI RAHUL SHEWALE (MUMBAI SOUTH CENTRAL): Mr. Chairman, Sir, thank you for giving me time to speak on Demands for Grants in respect of Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change. 

First of all, I would like to enlighten this august House on one of the important issues concerning the overall development of wildlife sanctuaries in the country. Many precious species of wildlife are on the verge of extinction due to negligence and poor planning for the last so many years. Amongst the other wildlife species, I had been drawing attention of the Government to the extinction of resident Gyps species of vultures in the country. The number of vultures of Gyps species is declining day by day due to negligence in their conservation. Some NGOs like Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS) are working for conservation of vultures in the country in collaboration with the State Governments. Breeding Centres of vultures are being set up by the BNHS at various places in Haryana, Rajasthan and other States.

In the absence of financial aid from the Central Government, the maintenance and development work of the breeding centres are not going on well. The BNHS has also submitted its detailed proposal for conservation of vultures to the Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change for grant of Central financial assistance to implement their programme in the country which is awaiting approval for long.

In this connection, I would like to submit that multi-dose of veterinary use of some medicines like declofenac is also one of the reasons for extinction of this precious Gyps Vulture. I suggest immediate ban on sale of multi-dose vials of declofenac medicine which may be imposed to prevent its misuse in cattle treatment in the country.

My request to the Minister of Environment, Forests and Climate Change is to look into the matter seriously and raise the financial aid to the States and NGOs who are working for the noble cause of preservation and protection of wild species, especially conservation of vultures in the country.

There are many important issues of my constituency Mumbai South-Central which are pending for a long time for environment clearance with the Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change. I would like to point out some of them briefly.

The first is the construction of a coastal road in Mumbai. Most of the coastal lines in various cities in the country are having coastal roads, whereas the most important city of Mumbai does not have it so far. Mumbai has a beautiful coastline. There is a dire need for construction of a 36-kilometre road along the coastline by reclamation in sea. This is pending due to non-clearance by the Environment Ministry for a long time. It should be expedited immediately.

Another issue is of modification of policy guidelines for implementation of slum rehabilitation scheme in CRZ-II areas. Comprehensive proposals are being submitted by the Maharashtra State Government to allow increase in permissible FSI in the slum rehabilitation schemes in CRZ-II areas at par with those in non-CRZ areas for development of slum areas in Mumbai. I request the Minister of Environment, Forests and Climate Change for early action and finalise the modification of policy guidelines for implementation of slum rehabilitation schemes in CRZ-II areas in Greater Mumbai.

Sir, the Law Minister was here and the other point is regarding one very abused law and it is about the 2006 law where a tribal can actually claim right over the Forest land. I think, the Government needs to be innovative and it has to be pragmatic also because if the Government follows the UN, then they say that India has to spend 500 billion dollars for environment protection and that is not going to happen.
