*SHRI LADU KISHORE SWAIN (ASKA):The Union Budget 2015-16 has allocated Rs.1682 crore as the total budget for the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, which wars Rs.2256 crore in the previous year. This indicates 25 per cent budget cut in this year. Within this reduced budget, now government is thinking of ensuring clean environment that includes, water, air, soil etc. The recently released Intergovernmental Panel on Climate change (IPCC) synthesis report suggests to increasingly internalize climate considerations into development planning in developing countries. The effects of global warming on the Indian subcontinent vary from the submergence of low-lying island and coastal lands to the melting of glaciers in the Indian Himalayas, threatening the volumetric flow rate of many of the most important rivers of India and South Asia. In India, such effects are projected to impact millions of lives ( as has been seen in recent earthquake in Northern part of India).

In this regard, it is important to highlight that the Union Budget 2014-15 had created 100 crore National Adaptation Fund (NAF). Guidelines to operationalise this Fund are still awaited. Meanwhile, India has begun accessing funds from the Global Adaptation Fund and is ready for the Green Climate Fund (GCF) when the later is operationalized.

It is in this context that I would like to draw the attention of the Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change to consider following climate change issues in the budgetary provisions.

The share of Ministry of New and Renewable Energy ( MNRE) in National Clean Energy Fund (NCEF) transfers to various ministries was 80 per cent in Union Budget 2013-14 Revised Estimates. This share was reduced to 34 per cent in Union Budget 2014-15. This decline is largely due to transfer of Rs.1500 crore from NCEF to support National Ganga Plan under the Ministry of Water Resources. This raises a concern as to whether there could be a further decline in allocation for MNRE from the NCEF because of the financial requirements to address other pressing issues. Further, for the National Afforestation Programme, the Union Budget allocation for 2015-16 declined from Rs.235 crore in 2014-15 to Rs.75 crore with a plea of larger devolution of resources to the states. This has been a major concern in view of the positive impact that it has created in the past.

This is the first time that the Indian government has categorically earmarked domestic funds for adaptation. The National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC, 2008) did sate that India spent 2.63 percent of the GDP in 2006-07 on adaptation programmes in five areas but no figures were given for subsequent years. The five areas mentioned for 2006-07 were: (a) crop improvement and research (5.93 per cent); (b) drought proofing and flood control (3.04 per cent); (c) forest conservation (0.49 per cent); (d) poverty alleviation and livelihoods preservation (44.65 per cent); (e) rural education and infrastructure (26.85 per cent); (f) health (10.75 per cent); (g) risk financing (4.83 per cent); and (h) disaster management (3.46 per cent). It has not been possible to de-construct these budgetary proportions to decipher what adaptation initiatives were funded or to what extent they reduced vulnerabilities to climate variability and built people's resilience. Probably these budgets were for business-as-usual activities under ongoing programmes that aim to safeguard a country that is anyway highly vulnerable to disasters and, as an agrarian society, is exceedingly dependent on temperature and rainfall patterns for its survival.

Subsequent to the release of the NAPCC, none of the adaptation-focused National Missions (pertaining to agriculture, water resources, forests and scientific knowledge), nor the State-level Action Plans on Climate Change (SAPCCs) that p-rioritise adaptation, have come up with clear budgets to support adaptation activities across sectors.,

Increase the corpus and broaden the scope of the National Adaptation Fund (NAF) so that it adds value to ongoing 'business-as-usual' development programems and/or activities in a transparent and measurable manner, rather than fund stand-alone adaptation projects. 

Make climate change adaptation core to India's financial planning for development with all climate-sensitive ministries/State departments ear-marking a clear and measurable proportion of their spending towards building resilient components in their programmes.

Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change issued order on 28 October 2014 pertaining to diversion of forest land for non-forest purposes under the Forest (Conservation) Act 1980 and STs and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act 2006, which had now exempted State Government from taking prior consent from Gram Sabhas for projects where linear diversion of use of Forest land is involved. Further to this, in case of plantations which were notified as forest on a day less than 75 years prior to the 13th December 2005 and are located in villages having no recorded population of Scheduled Tribes as per Census 2001 and Census 2011, no forest rights are likely to be recognized and only a certificate from the concerned District Collector will be sufficient without any consent from Gram Sabhas. Such an order will be counter-productive for sustainable development and is opposed to the participatory nature of the decision making process. Hence, we demand the government to reverse such orders which discards specific provisions in the Forests Right Act, 2006 which seeks 'prior informed consent' of Gram Sabhas before acquiring forest land clearing of forests for non-forest activity.

This order is released after taking consent from Ministry of Tribal Affairs, which raises concerns that whether the nodal ministry for Tribal Affairs carried out due diligence before giving such consent as there seems an ignorance of rights of tribal communities.

Order also allows for forest clearance for linear diversion of forest land such as highways, pipelines, rail tracks etc. which will cause an infringement in ecological balance of forests and may lead to rapid depletion of India' forest cover due to possible start-up of other related business activities along these linear projects in future. There is need to review this order with inclusion of cumulative impact assessment process of proposed project in view of future scenarios, along with following a participatory decision making process.

In a country where the economy is inextricably tied to climate-sensitive resources at several levels, Rs.100 crore as a national adaptation budget is just notional. This needs to be scaled up and rationalized with external funds for adaptation provided under UNFCCC and through bilateral and multilateral aid.

There is a need for capacity and skill building on better assessment of climate vulnerabilities and delivery of adaptation interventions at all levels and across all sectors- health, education, livelihoods and disaster mitigation and rehabilitation. This would include, for instance, skill in collection of climate data (including, for example, from panchayat and village-level rain gauges), assessing risks and monitoring adaptation outputs and outcomes.

The developmental budgets in agriculture, rural development and health saw drastic decline in the allocation in Union Budget 2015-16. These are the most vulnerable sectors to climate change and require robust developmental budgets with additional adaptation financing. With the creation of the National Adaptation Fund, it is high time to introduce sectoral monitoring of financial outlays based on common databases and facilitated by GIS techniques.

श्री पी.पी. चौधरी (पाली)ः मैं सरकार का ध्यान राजस्थान राज्य की सबसे प्रदू­िात नदी की ओर आकर्­िात करते हुए बताना चाहूंगा कि मेरे लोक सभा क्षेत्र की बांड़ी नदी व नेहडा बांध लगातार भयानक रूप से प्रदू­िात होते जा रहे हैं। वर्तमान में स्थिति बद् से बद्तर हो रही है। पीने के लिए भू-जल का पानी खराब हो चुका है। पानी के किनारे बसने वाले पशु-पक्षी भी नगण्य के बराबर दिखते हैं, क्योंकि वे भी जानते हैं, इस पानी को पीने के बाद उनकी मृत्यु तय है।

इस संबंध में राज्य सरकार, उच्च न्यायालय, राज्य मानवाधिकार आयोग, राज्य प्रदू­ाण नियंत्रण मंडल व केन्द्रीय ग्रीन ट्रिब्यूनल आदि के द्वारा उठाए गए कदम व दिए गए निर्देश नाकाफी रहे हैं। यहां रहने वाले लोगों के स्वास्थ्य में भी निरंतर गिरावट देखी जा सकती है। पाली जिले के किसानों की जमीन बंजर होती जा रही है और यदि उस जमीन पर कुछ उग भी आता है तो उसकी गुणवत्ता बहुत ही निचली किस्म की होती है, जिसे बाजार भाव में बेचा जाना संभव नहीं होता। राज्य पशुपालन विभाग की रिपोर्ट के अनुसार यहां विचरण करने वाली पशुओं में बांझपन, प्रतिरोधक क्षमता व उत्पादन क्षमता में कमी आदि दर्ज की गई है। हालांकि प्रदू­ाण नियंत्रण करने के अनेक उपायों पर विचार किया जा चुका है, जो काफी नहीं रहे। 

इस गम्भीर समस्या का निदान किया जा सकता है, लेकिन उसकी लागत बहुत अधिक है राज्य सरकार और औद्योगिक इकाइयां इसे वहन करने में असक्षम है। केन्द्र सरकार द्वारा इस संबंध में आवश्यक बजट जारी करने के बाद ही इस समस्या को दूर किया जा सकता है।

अतः मेरा माननीय जल संसाधन मंत्री एवं पर्यावरण मंत्री जी से अनुरोध है कि केन्द्र सरकार द्वारा विशे­ाज्ञों की टीम को राजस्थान के पाली जिले में भेजा जाए ताकि पाली जिले की इस गम्भीर समस्या को दूर करने के लिए केन्द्र सरकार द्वारा विस्तृत योजना तैयार की जा सके। 

मैं अरावली पर्वत श्रृंखला के उस भाग की ओर भी ध्यान आकर्­िात करना चाहूंगा जो कि राजस्थान के मरूस्थलीय क्षेत्र से होकर गुजरता है। इसके अंतर्गत राजस्थान के जोधपुर, जैसलमेर, बाड़मेर, बीकानेर, जयपुर आदि जिले आते हैं। पहले से ही राजस्थान में पेड़ों की भारी कमी है और अरावली पर्वत श्रृंखला पर पेड़ों की रक्षा के लिए कोई उपाय ना होने से दिन-प्रतिदिन पेड़ नहीं के बराबर दिखाई देने लगे हैं। जिससे पर्यावरण को भारी नुकसान पहुंच रहा है और इसकी मार राजस्थान ही नहीं बल्कि पूरा हिन्दुस्तान झेल रहा है। मानसून की अनियमित और अनिश्चितता इसका एक उदाहरण है। यदि सरकार ने इस संबंध में कोई गम्भीर उपाय नहीं किए तो इसका दु­परिणाम जल्द ही भुगतान होगा।

मैं इस संबंध में माननीय मंत्री जी से यह निवेदन करना चाहता हूं कि वे अरावली पर्वत श्रृंखला पर, विशे­ाकर राजस्थान के क्षेत्र में वृक्षारोपण के लिए विशे­ा कदम उठाएं तथा पर्वतों पर वृक्षों की हो रही अवैध कटाई को रोकने के लिए भी उपाय करें। 

इसी के साथ, वन एवं पर्यावरण मंत्रालय के लिए प्रस्तुत मांगों का मैं समर्थन करता हूं। 

*SHRI R. DHRUVANARAYANA (CHAMARAJANAGAR): The importance of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change cannot be overstated enough in today's age. Given the impact of Climate change on agriculture that affects over 60% of our population and the devastating natural calamities that have happened in recent years, it is imperative that we focus on this sector. The same approach was underlined in the 12th Five Year Plan which recommended huge allocations, but that is not reflected in the budget. Up till 2013-14, allocation had been increasing every year for the Ministry, however from 2014 onwards a complete shift in trend has happened. In 2014-15, the Government reduced allocation by 13%. Now, this year the Government has reduced the allocation again by 19%. This is absolutely worrying in the face of the challenges before us.

The Government has allocated Rs.137.06 crore for Tiger Projects, as compared to Rs. 161.92 crore allotted last year. This is a decrease of 15% from last year. This is extremely unfortunate as tiger is the national animal of our country. Yet the population of tigers in the Country as on 2014, is only 2,226. Although, the population has increased in recent years, experts believe that this 30% increase is partly due to counting errors in previous years. As per data by the Wildlife Protection Society of India, at least 110 tigers were killed in 2011-14, barely a drop from the 118 poached in 2007-10. We have 70% of the world's wild tigers on less than 25% of the world's tiger habitat. This itself suggests that we must sustain our effort to protect and conserve this habitat.

In my constituency, Chamarajnagar, there are two tiger projects being run by the government-Bandipur National Park and Tiger Reserve, and BRT Project at both these Tiger Projects. There is need for the Government's support to maintain and protect the increased population of tigers. Various experts have also called for the Government to come forward on this front.

There is also increasing number of instances of casualties caused due to human animal conflict across the country. The data of such instances is not maintained centrally but the Ministry has accepted the problem. In such instances, people who live closest to reserves, that is the tribal population is most affected. There are two issues in the Government's efforts. First is the issue of compensation being provided by the government in cases where people are killed in human animal conflict. At present, the Government is providing Rs.2 lacks as compensation under Project Tiger. However, this is not sufficient. I urge the Minister to increase this compensation. Secondly, at present, the Government's approach on human-animal conflict is more reactive than preventive. The issue requires concern effort of the Government focused on prevention of such instances. There is a need for more allocations towards solar fencing and awareness, so that the risk of human-animal conflict can be mitigated. I urge the Minister to take appropriate steps on the issue. 

The Forest Rights Act, 2006 has been implemented since 2008, and provides rights to forest dwellers to own, access and take decisions regarding the forest area. Under FRA the Gram Sabha regulates access to forest resources and can stop any activity, which adversely affects the forest.

The Government recently laid down that instead of tribal village councils certifying that their rights had been settled and they had consented to projects, the district administrations would be empowered to do so in 60 days, regardless of the number of villages affected by the projects. On 28th October 2014, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change had sent out a letter to all States giving rights to the District administration to divert forest area for other purposes.

Even the Tribal Ministry has written repeatedly to the Ministry of Environment and Forest on the issue. As per reports, the Tribal Affairs Secretary, has written that there was no proof that the Forest Rights Act was delaying projects. The letter clearly mentions that the Ministry of Environment and Forest is short-circuiting the legal process of consent.

For tribals, across the country, the Forests Rights Act is the most important tool for empowerment. These are the communities that suffer most due to degradation of natural resources. This dilution, gives a message that the government is not concerned about the peace and governance of forest areas. I urge the Minister to withdraw any such notifications that dilute the Act. Clearances for environment and forest must not come at the compromise of tribal rights.

As per a report by the World Health Organization (WHO), Delhi's air pollution is the highest in the World. Besides this, as many as 13 Indian cities are the top 20 cities in terms of air pollution. As per reports from all over the World, the link between high air pollution and health concerns is clear -cut. One study by top universities in the US has claimed that Indians are losing on an average 3 years of their life span because of high air pollution. It was in the light of this, that President Obama, on his recent visit to Delhi bought air purifiers, which were installed at the Republic Day Parad. The Ministry has been dismissive of these reports on health concerns. Would the Ministry, in this case commission an independent study on the matter so that the link between health risks and air pollution can be ascertained?

At the same time, the Ministry has stated to the Delhi High Court, that as of now, there is no action plan to tackle the issue of air pollution in Delhi. I urge the Ministry, to not only come up with an action plan for Delhi but also for cities that are facing an air pollution crisis. This includes Bangalore, Delhi, Agra, Kanpur, Lucknow, Varanasi, Faridabad, Ahmedabad, Chennai and Hyderabad.

The Government has recently launched National Air Quality Index (NAQI) for monitoring air quality across 10 cities. However, in three cities the data has been found to be insufficient to monitor air quality. Across these cities, monitoring infrastructure has been found to be lacking. In some cities only one monitoring station exists while various monitoring stations are unfunctional. I urge the Minister to look into these issues so that the monitoring initiative is successful and does not merely exist on paper.

SHRI P.V. MIDHUN REDDY (RAJAMPET): Mr. Chairman, Sir, thank you. Every civilized society has a responsibility to take care of its environment and forest. In a developing country like India we have seen how human greed has affected our forest cover and our environment. Although our forest cover has been increasing at the rate of 0.46 per cent from year 2000 till now, it is not substantial and we need to increase our forest cover. Though the social awareness level has been growing, the actual impact is very less. The 14th Finance Commission has allocated 7.5 per cent for increasing the forest cover. It is a welcome move. This 7.5 per cent is by way of devolution of union taxes to States. What we need is negative incentives so that the States are under pressure to increase their forest cover. 

In my constituency, Rajampet, which is in Andhra Pradesh, we have 80 per cent of the world’s red sanders tree. This is in the Seshachalam forest area. Red sanders is in the endangered list of our Central Government. Each tonne of red sanders cost Rs. 24 lakh to even Rs. 1 crore. This is the reason why a lot of smuggling is happening. These trees are being felled very rampantly. The Government is unable to control the smuggling of this red sanders. Recently the Central Government has given permission to auction and sell the confiscated red sanders. 

We request the Central Government to step in and control the smuggling of the red sanders. The proceeds of this auction should be used for development of the red sanders, protecting the forest cover and protecting the red sanders throughout the State. It should not be diverted for other purposes. We also request that a comprehensive National Policy on sand mining should be there. Extensive mining of sand is depleting water resources and creating an imbalance in our ecology and environment, especially in the Rayalaseema Region, there has been a huge depletion of water table. The Government should look for alternative sources of resources which can replace sand. There must be a balance between environment and development. Faster economic growth is directly proportional to reduction of poverty. For this, our country has to grow at 10 per cent in the coming years. To sustain this 10 per cent growth, we need huge investments in infrastructure and various other manufacturing industries. We have no choice but to increase our power capacity by close to two lakh MW in the coming five years. Under pressure from the NGOs and people with vested interests, many large aluminium, steel, cement and thermal projects, for which initial clearances were given, have been stalled. This is not good for our country in the global scenario. Uncertainties like this will discourage people from coming to India. 

Now, we are having slogans like “Make in India” but it will be a far-fetched reality if we do not act in time and clear all these uncertainties. Even our former Prime Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh said in one of his statements that NGOs funded by foreign companies try to stall the Koodankulam Power Project. If such is the case, we should know that even other projects would have been stalled by vested interests. At a time when we must be growing, we find projects with huge investments are stuck for environmental and forest clearances.… (Interruptions)

Unfortunately, it is the nationalised banks and small investors who put in their life savings into these companies who are at stake. No person would oppose genuine steps to protect environment, particularly the tribal people who are dependent on the forests. But if we have economic and strategic mines in the tribal areas, we should definitely make use of these resources and use the profits for the development of the tribal people.

Coming to forests, the BK Chaturvedi Committee dealing with coal block allocations observed that only 0.75 per cent of the total forest cover is required for giving clearances to all the coal blocks of the country. The Committee also observed that it can power two lakh MW of power in our country. It suggested that instead of stopping mining, the Government can impose a tax on these mines and afforest at least 100 more degraded forests in our country.

I would conclude by saying that our Party has cautioned in the past and we are saying it again that unless the PMO, where all the Union Ministries converge, has a mechanism to monitor all major projects on a daily basis ensuring that all inter-Ministerial clearances are given on time, we will be back to square one. All our good intentions and aspirations will just remain on paper and Achhe Din will be very far away.

श्री नारणभाई काछड़िया (अमरेली)ः जलवायु परिवर्तन प्रत्यक्ष और परोक्ष रूप से मानवीय गतिविधियों के कारण होता है और यह परिवर्तन विश्व वातावरण की संरचना को बदल देता है। पृथ्वी की जलवायु हमेशा बदलती और विकसित होती रही है। इस प्रकार के कुछेक परिवर्तन प्राकृतिक कारणों से होते हैं लेकिन अन्य के लिए मानवीय क्रियाकलाप जिम्मेदार होते है, जैसे पेड़ों की कटाई, उद्योगों तथा परिवहन से वायुमंडलीय उत्सर्जन, जिसके कारण वायुमंडल में गैस तथा ऐरोसॉल्स एकत्रित हो जाते हैं। इन गैसों को ग्रीनहाऊस गैस कहते हैं क्योंकि ये गर्मी को रोक लेती है और धरातल के निकट वायु के तापमान को बढ़ा देती है और पृथ्वी की सतह पर ग्रीनहाउस की भूमिका अदा करती है।

ग्लोबल वार्मिंग ने समुद्री स्तर, बर्फ की चादर तथा व­ााऩ को प्रभावित करना शुरू कर दिया है। हवा के तापमान में बढ़ोतरी द्वारा जलवायु के क्षेत्रीय पैटर्न में होने वाले परिवर्तन ने विश्व के कई भागों में जल संभरण तथा पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र को प्रभावित करना पहले ही शुरू कर दिया है। यह बढ़ता हुआ तापमान और बढ़ता हुआ समुद्र स्तर मीठे पानी की उपलब्धता, समुद्री खारेपन, खाद्य उत्पादन को प्रभावित कर सकता है। यह तटीय क्षेत्रों को जलमग्न कर सकती है और जलजनित विकारों का प्रकोप बढ़ सकता है।

जलवायु परिवर्तन विकास के समक्ष एक बड़ा खतरा है, जो गरीबी मिटाने और समृद्धि को जनता में बांटने के प्रयासों को कमजोर कर सकता है। अगर कोई मजबूत और त्वरित कार्रवाई नहीं की जाती है, तो धरती के तापमान में डेढ़ से दो डिग्री की वृद्धि हो सकती है। इसकी वहज बीते समय और वर्तमान समय में ग्रीनहाउस गैसों का उत्सर्जन है। इस तापमान बढ़ोतरी के चलते समुद्र के जलस्तर में वृद्धि और चक्रवातों के जल्दी-जल्दी आने का खतरा बढ़ रहा है। मात्र दो डिग्री की वृद्धि से ब्राजील की सोयाबीन फसल का उत्पादन 70 फीसदी तक कम हो सकती है। दो डिग्री की वृद्धि से दुनिया में मक्का, गेहूं और अंगूर की फसलों के उत्पादन में 50 फीसदी की कमी आ सकती है। उत्तरी रूस में इसके कारण बर्फ के ढके क्षेत्र में लगातार बर्फ पिघलेगी जिसके चलते नुकसानदायक मीथेन गैस के उत्सर्जन में वृद्धि होगी।

वैश्विक तापवृद्धि से निपटने हेतु संभावित उपायों में शामिल हैः रसोई गैस सब्सिडी को केवल जरूरतमंद लोगों तक सीमित रखा जाना जिससे कच्चे तेल के आयात में कटौती सम्भव है। एलईडी के इस्तेमाल करने पर देश में कई अरब यूनिट बिजली की बचत हो सकती है। सरकारी बैंक देश में ग्रीन एनर्जी जैसे सोलर एवं विंड एनर्जी को प्रमोट करने के लिए सस्ता एवं सुविधाजनक लोन उपलब्ध कराए। हरित कानूनों को सख्ती से लागू किया जाना चाहिए। हमारे देश की लगातार बढ़ती जनसंख्या को देखते हुए हमें अन्य नवीकरणीय ऊर्जा प्रौद्योगिकीय कार्यक्रम की सम्भावनाओं को तलाशनें की जरूरत है। सार्वजनिक परिवहन प्रणाली को अपनाए जाने से भी प्रदू­ाण का स्तर कम करके उत्सर्जन में कमी लाई जा सकती है। भारत में मनरेगा जैसी रा­ट्रीय स्तर की योजना को ग्रीन इंडिया मिशन से जोड़े जाने से जलवायु परिवर्तन द्वारा वैश्विक तापवृद्धि पर रोक लगाई जा सकती है।

अब समय आ गया है कि जलवायु परिवर्तन के कारण होने वाले वैश्विक तापवृद्धि से मुकाबला करने के लिए पर्यावरण हितै­ााळ और कम कार्बन उत्सर्जन करने वाले शहर विकसित करने पर जोर दिया जाए तथा संभाव्य जलवायु सम्बंधी खतरों से सुरक्षित रहने के लिए समयबद्ध आवश्यक कार्यवाही की जाए।

*SHRI B.N. CHANDRAPPA (CHITRADURGA): I think this Government is attaching scant attention to this Ministry, which is very vital for sustainable development. To me this Ministry is very important. What is happening now is that the industrially developed countries of the West are trying to impose environmental norms on our country. So, the main question is of striking a balance.

This puts India among the very few countries that have included financial mechanisms like carbon tax in their strategies to deal with the threat of climate change. *SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE (BARAMATI): The allocation for the Ministry of Environment and Forest accounts for Rs 1681 crores, a 25% percent decrease from the budget estimate of the 2014-15 and even below the revised estimate of 2014-15. The whole forestry and wildlife department was granted Rs. 362.84 crore, a staggering 21% less than what it was allocated in the previous financial year.

The allocation for Project Tiger, India's most celebrated wildlife conservation programme, Rs. 136 Crore, a decrease of around 15% from Rs. 161 Crore in 2014-15. The All India Tiger Estimation Report released in January said the tiger population had increased by 30% from 2010 to 2,226 in 2014. It was only through the efforts of 3 years of UPA and NDA have helped us to achieve this state. By cutting allocation, we do not want to go back to the situation. I have recently visited Tadoba and was amazed to see how it has created a lot of wealth and livelihood for the people.

Forest rangers, deputy forest rangers, foresters and forest guards are the frontline field level staff working for the protection and conservation of precious forest and wildlife wealth of our country. They are the interactive interface of the forest department with the public. While their job is tough and demanding and it involves high risk, they are poorly paid, underequipped, untrained and consequently de-motivated. Add to that they live deprived from basic facilities like clean drinking water, toilets, electricity, communication systems, protective rain/winter gear and medical aid.

According to me, this would dilute the campaign to save tigers and pave the way for clearance of industrial projects near tiger sanctuaries. Tigers are found across 17 states in India, whereas lion is found in only one. India is home to more than 2,200 tigers, whereas the Asiatic lion population, estimated at 411, is confined to Gujarat's Gir. If we really want to make lion the national animal, you should first restore at least 10-15 natural habitats which are suitable for lions. Then the lions should be relocated there from Gir.

The International Union for Conservation of Nature's Red List, lists 374 species in India as vulnerable and 274 others as endangered, or critically endangered, and at risk of becoming extinct. From well-known mammals like elephants, leopards, rhinos to numerous less-known animals, such as pangolins, tortoises and geckos all are endangered in our country. There are just 26,000 and 30,000 elephants left in the wild in India. The agency has recorded the loss of over 120 elephants due to poaching between 2008 and 2011. During the same period, WPSI has records to seizure of 781 kg ivory and 69 tusks, besides ivory pieces and carved articles. Poaching and smuggling present a huge threat to the wildlife. WPSI, a wildlife conservation organisation, has recorded over 20,000 wildlife crime cases. It is utmost important to create a safe environment to our wildlife also. I here also like to ask the Minister for the rationale for doing such drastic cut in the allocation to Central Zoo Authority from Rs 27.50 Crore to Rs 5.8 Crore. I am also worried that budgetary allocation to Indian council of Forestry research and education has been continuously decreasing. It was Rs 160.26 Crore in BE 2013-14, Rs 156.66 Crore in BE 2014-15 and now has been brought down to Rs 125.60 Crore. The council was set up with an objective to achieve the national goals of conserving forest area and to take care of the research needs. It is imperative to provide ample amount of resources to an institute of such importance.

Now talking about air pollution, I felt really sad when I read in the news piece that because of low level of Air quality, there was a speculation that the US authorities here could seek to curtail Obama's "outdoor activities" during his visit. It is said that Obama lost 6 hours of his life because he stayed in Delhi. This speaks volume of the seriousness of the situation. Industrialization and environment needs to go hand in hand. 90 per cent of coal-based thermal power plants in India fare unsatisfactorily on the environmental front. Infact the best coal plants in India are average in terms of environment performance when compared to their counterparts worldwide. There is also a need to produce clean energy. Target of renewable energy capacity has been revised to 175000 MW till 2022. Though the targets are very impressive, I am doubtful of meeting the targets especially when the cut to renewable energy sector to a mere Rs 303 crore from over Rs 550 crore in the revised budget 2014-15.

I would also like to bring attention of the Government to the concept of light pollution. Light pollution is a side effect of industrial civilization. Its sources include building exterior and interior lighting, advertising, commercial properties, offices, factories, streetlights, and illuminated sporting venues. It not only degrade photic habitat like bats, owl but also proves to be a major astronomical disruption. Awareness in this regard is extremely important. Government in public assets atleast should use full-cut off shielding in light fixtures which is the essential remedy. A lamp should send all its light more or less down where the light is intended to be used, not upward or sideways.

India generates about 60 million tonnes of trash every year. Ten million tonnes of garbage is generated in just the metropolitan cities. The landfills of most of these cities are already overflowing, with no space to accommodate fresh garbage waste. Constructing new landfill sites is one solution but more importantly the Government should be looking into innovative methods to dispose and recycle its waste. The reason why most landfill sites are over-flowing is because the current waste disposal system is inefficient. There are waste management plants, but they are not running at full capacity mainly due to the lack of waste segregation that has made waste management problematic. Segregation at source is the only solution. Recyclable waste like construction and demolition waste, organic waste like household garbage, toxic waste like medical waste, are all mixed together. The segregation of biodegradable waste from non-biodegradable waste is not done properly. Segregation of waste should occur at the colony or neighborhood level, when the waste is collected. Effective management of garbage is extremely important as it affects the health of our citizens in an extremely severe manner. Nearly 20% of methane gas emissions in India are caused by landfills. Due to the decomposition of inorganic waste, the ground water is contaminated. There is also the problem of leachate when rainfall percolates through the waste in a landfill.

Swach Bharat Abhiyan currently encourages citizens to not pollute the cities and make more use of dustbin to drive cleanliness. But awareness of segregation of degradable and non-degradable substance is still a distant dream. Before cleaning up the city, the government needs to sort out a concrete waste management system that ensures segregation and recycling. Process everything that can be processed and dump only the residue in the landfill. I would urge the government to expand the scope of the mission and start spreading awareness on the importance of waste segregation along with the cleanliness drive itself.

Furthermore the Central Board of Excise and Customs (CBEC, MoF, GoI) rather seems to be against the 'Swacch Bharat Abhiyan' as CBEC is denying the legally valid input tax credit on services used for making a Secured Landfill (SLF) to Waste Management entities in India. Rule 2 (1) of CENVAT Credit Rules, 2004 provides definition of input services means any service used by a provider of output service for providing an output service excluding construction or execution of works contract of a building or a civil structure or a part thereof. As you are aware, SLF is created as per Pollution Control Board Guidelines for dumping waste, it is neither a building nor a civil structure. So, simply speaking, Waste Management Entities, which are paying service tax on their service income, cannot claim credit on sources which are used by them. This denial of input tax credit means higher cost to Waste Management Entities. Given the above, can the Government set their internal department (CBEC) in order before telling others to follow the 'Swachh Bharat Abhiyan'.

श्री जय प्रकाश नारायण यादव:  सभापति महोदय, कृ­ण भगवान ने अपनी मां से कहा था कि मइया तुम इन्द्र की पूजा मत करो, लेकिन मां नहीं मानी, पिता नहीं माने। जब कृ­ण जी आठ साल के बालक थे, तब उन्होंने कहा कि गोवर्धन पर्वत की पूजा कीजिए। उन्होंने कहा कि तुम क्या बोल रहे हो? उस समय इन्द्र भगवान ने अपना प्रकोप दिखाया। हमारे पास इतना समय नहीं है, इसलिए हम अपनी पूरी बात नहीं बोल पायेंगे। इन्द्र भगवान ने अपना सारा प्रकोप दिखाया, लेकिन कृ­ण भगवान ने अपनी छोटी अंगुली पर गोवर्धन पर्वत उठा लिया और कहा कि इन्द्र भगवान को जितना भी घमंड है, उसे प्रकृति तोड़ेगी, पहाड़ तोड़ेगा और जनता तोड़ेगी। उस समय इन्द्र भगवान हारे थे। हमारा कहना है कि प्रकृति के साथ छेड़छाड़ नहीं होनी चाहिए। प्रकृति शाश्वत है, निरंतर है। आज मौसम में बदलाव हो रहा है। प्रकृति अजय है और हम उसके जीव हैं। लेकिन आज जीव प्रकृति के साथ छेड़छाड़ कर रहा है। हमें प्रकृति का आदर करना चाहिए, उसके आंचल के नीचे रहना चाहिए, लेकिन आज हम कुदरत के साथ छेड़छाड़ कर रहे हैं। वन, वृक्ष लगाने से हमारे पर्यावरण में सुधार हो सकता है। झील खत्म हो रही हैं। माननीय सदस्य कह रहे थे कि राजस्थान में झीलों का नुकसान हुआ है, तालाबों का नुकसान हुआ है। पहाड़ रक्षक हैं, भक्षक नहीं हैं। प्रकृति के साथ छेड़छाड़ करेंगे तो मालथस थ्योरी लागू हो जाएगी। भूकम्प आया, नेपाल से बिहार तक विनाशकारी लीला हुई। ये सब प्रकृति के साथ छेड़छाड़ करने से हुआ है। उत्तराखंड, जम्मू-कश्मीर में ऐसा हुआ है। बाढ़ के समय सूखा और सूखे के समय बाढ़ आ जाती है। ग्लोबल वार्मिंग हो रही है, जलवायु में परिवर्तन हो रहा है। नवीनतम प्रयोग हो रहे हैं, वैज्ञानिक अध्ययन कर रहे हैं कि मौसम क्यों बिगड़ रहा है। शहरीकरण हो रहा है, इसे रोकने की जरूरत है। जनसंख्या का बोझ बढ़ता जा रहा है। बर्फ की चादर खराब होती जा रही है। कार्बन बढ़ता जा रहा है, पेड़ काटे जा रहे हैं, हमें पेड़ लगाने हैं। पेड़ हमारा भवि­य है। सरकारी संस्था और गैर सरकारी संस्थाओं द्वारा स्कूलों में पर्यावरण की पढ़ाई पर जोर देना चाहिए। पर्यावरण के लिए लाइसेंस दे रहे हैं, लेकिन इससे कुछ ठीक नहीं होगा, इंस्पेक्टर राज से कुछ ठीक नहीं होगा। वातावरण के सही निर्माण करने से ही रा­ट्र को बेहतर बना सकते हैं। पर्यावरण को ठीक रखना हर आदमी का कर्तव्य है। फसल की बर्बादी हो रही है, जमीन की बर्बादी हो रही है। जल में आर्सेनिक और फ्लोराइड आ रहा है। जान पर खतरा बन रहा है। कैसे मेक इन इंडिया बनेगा? कैसे स्वच्छ भारत बनेगा? कैसे स्वस्थ भारत बनेगा? जब तक वन के साथ छेड़छाड़ होती रहेगी, वन के साथ छेड़छाड़ होती रहेगी, कुछ ठीक नहीं होगा। 

बिहार में बाल्मिकी नगर, भीम बांध, बांका, लक्खीसराय में प्राकृतिक छटा का बहुत प्रभाव है। आज रा­ट्र का पर्यावरण बिगड़ रहा है, मौसम भी बिगड़ रहा है। रा­ट्र का पर्यावरण जनता ठीक करेगी और मौसम को हम मिलजुल कर ठीक करेंगे। 

कबीर दास की उलटी वाणी, बरसे कंबल भीगे पानी।

वन, पर्यावरण, जलवायु का मिजाज बिगड़ रहा है। इस पर विशे­ा ध्यान देना होगा। मैं इन्हीं शब्दों के साथ अपनी बात समाप्त करता हूं। धन्यवाद।

SHRI DHARAM VIRA GANDHI (PATIALA): Thank you, Sir, for giving me the opportunity to speak on this important topic. When the entire world is talking about global warming, environmental degradation and climatic changes which endangers to the mother Earth Planet, I am very sorry to say that the number of members present in this august House is very small. This should be the matter of concern for all of us. 

Many hon. Members have touched this topic from many angles. I think, they all have touched only from fringes of this topic. I would like to touch it through my brief address and through the basics of this issue. The fact of the matter is that present model of development which we call the capitalist model of development has come in direct contradiction with the mother Earth Planet and with its environment. 

The capitalist model of development means profit. It is ruthless both for the human as well as for the natural resources. Therefore in its continuous pursuit of profit, the capitalism ruthlessly exploits not only the human resources, but natural resources as well. It has taken the toll of human resources, it has taken the toll of natural resources, it has taken the toll of our value system and it has taken the toll of very great professions like teaching and medicine. It has taken the toll of environment on this earth. The basic problem of environmental degradation is the present mode of production which has come in contradiction with the very nature itself. Either this model will persist or nature will remain there. So, this is the basic problem, which I would like to touch and it should be taken from that angle. 

Secondly, Dr. Michael Chadwick, a well known environmentalist and a noble prize nominee, a few years back, in a Summit on the "Sustainability of Mother of Planet and Population Growth on this Earth", said that it is the developed economies which are culprits for environmental degradation and not the backward economies or the backward countries like us. The biggest parameter as to how much this mother earth planet is endangered depends upon the Resource Demand Index, (RDI) i.e. how much thrust or pressure is on the natural resources from a particular country. The Resource Demand Index of India is 0.25 per cent whereas the Resource Demand Index of the United States of America is 4.17 per cent. They consume 17 times more than the Indian consumers. 

We, the people from Third World Countries, the Third Word Societies are very conservative. My mother used to keep an empty tin of oil, safe in our store to be used sometime later for some other purpose. But the ‘use and throw’ culture, which is classic of the Western economy, is coming into India also. So, we should not pursue that model of development with blind eyes or with that speed. We should have our own innovations, our own indigenous ideas to take our economy forward according to our culture and according to our methods and our indigenous ways. 

At the end, I would like to say that in Copenhagen Conference, there was a huge banner raised by 20,000 people from sixty countries, cutting across continents saying “struggle for environment is struggle against capitalism’. 

If we have to maintain our environment, if we have to protect our mother earth planet, if we have to escape from global warming and environmental degradation and if we have to save humanity, we should not follow or we should follow very cautiously the capitalist model of development.

श्री प्रेम सिंह चन्दूमाजरा (आनंदपुर साहिब) : माननीय सभापति जी, यह बहुत ही महत्वपूर्ण मंत्रालय है और इस मंत्रालय के सामने चुनौतियां भी बहुत हैं तथा चिंताएं भी बहुत हैं। मैं समझता हूं कि चुनौती तो ग्लोबल वार्मिंग की ही बहुत बड़ी है, क्लाइमेट चेंज की है और अनएक्सपेक्टेड जो आपदाएं आती हैं, उनका सामना कैसे किया जाए, जैसे जम्मू-कश्मीर में पहले बाढ़ आई और पीछे अभी 14 प्रदेशों में बेमौसमी बारिश हुई। पिछले दिनों में नेपाल, बिहार, राजस्थान और उत्तर प्रदेश जैसे प्रदेशों में भूकम्प से नुकसान हुआ। इन मुश्किलों को भी चुनौतियों के तौर पर लेना होगा। 

दूसरे, जो मैं यह समझता हूं कि इस मंत्रालय में एक तरफ तो विकास की बात है और दूसरी ओर मानवीय जिंदगी की बात है। हमें उसको बैलेंस में रखकर चलना होगा। सबसे बड़ी चुनौती प्रदू­ाण की है। जब प्रदू­ाण होता है, जैसे हवा में, पानी में, जमीन में और खाद्य पदार्थों में प्रदू­ाण होता है तथा दूसरी ओर हमें विकास प्राप्ति के लिए भी प्रयत्न करने हैं, जैसे कैमिकल्स से भी प्रदू­ाण फैलता है, उसको कंट्रोल करना होगा। माननीय प्रधान मंत्री जी ने जैसे अभी सॉयल हैल्थ कार्ड की योजना चलाई है, मैं समझता हूं कि अगर यह योजना किसी तरह से पहले चली होती तो काफी नुकसान होने से बचा जा सकता था। केंसर और जिगर की बहुत सी बीमारियों को रोका जा सकता था। मैं समझता हूं कि विकास के साथ साथ क्लिअरेंस की भी बहुत जरूरत पड़ती है।ॊ मैं कहना नहीं चाहता लेकिन क्लियरेंस के नाम पर पिछली सरकार में जो ब्लैक-मेलिंग होती रही, उसके कारण बहुत से विकास के काम रुके। मैं माननीय मंत्री जी को बधाई देना चाहता हूं कि मंत्री जी उसमें रिलेक्सेशन लाए और इस वजह से विकास शुरू हुआ। मैं कहना चाहता हूं कि प्राथमिकता तो मानवीय जिंदगी को देनी ही चाहिए, किंतु विकास को भी देखने की जरूरत है। इसके लिए कोई अल्टरनेटिव सोचना होगा।

श्री प्रेम सिंह चन्दूमाजरा: महोदय, मैं कुछ सुझाव देना चाहता हूं। सड़क, अस्पताल, चैक डैम्स आदि चीजों की जरूरत होती है। उसके लिए जहां भी अल्टरनेटिव फोरेस्ट लैंड पड़ी हो, उसे दिया जा सकता है। मेरा संसदीय क्षेत्र सेमी-हिल एरिया है। वहां 40 परसेंट हिस्से में दफा-4, दफा-5 लगी हुई है। मैं अपने संसदीय क्षेत्र की बात आपको बता सकता हूं। दूसरे प्रदेशों हिमाचल या उत्तरांचल के बारे में मैं नहीं कह सकता हूं। हमारे वहां अच्छे जंगल नहीं हैं और जमीन खाली पड़ी है। वहां से हमें मिट्टी का एक ढेला भी नहीं उठाने दिया जाता है। जमीन किसान की है लेकिन वह वहां कुछ नहीं कर सकता है। मेरा सुझाव है कि आप दफा-4 और दफा-5 को उठा कर कंडीशन लगा सकते हैं कि इस एरिया में 40 परसेंट फॉरेस्ट लगाना जरूरी होगा, प्लान्टेशन करनी जरूरी होगी, 60 परसेंट प्लान्टेशन करनी जरूरी होगी। आप किसान से एफिडेविट ले सकते हैं। बाकी जमीन पर आप उसे खेती करने दीजिए, क्योंकि जमीन अब कम हो रही है। चेयरमैन साहब यह महत्वपूर्ण बात है, हमारे पंजाब में विस्फोटक स्थिति बनी हुई है। हमारे पास जमीन कम है। हम उस जमीन को कल्टीवेट कर पाएं, उसके लिए आप दोनों में बैलेंस रख कर कोई उपाय कर लें। 

दूसरी बात, जंगलों में से जंगली जानवर निकल कर मैदान में आ जाते हैं। किसानों की फसल का नुकसान हो रहा है और जानी नुकसान भी हो रहा है। जब हम कृ­िा मंत्री जी के पास जाते हैं, हमारी पंजाब सरकार ने एक योजना बना कर भेजी तो कृ­िा मंत्रालय ने कहा कि फॉरेस्ट मंत्रालय के पास जाओ। हमने दो सौ करोड़ रुपये की मांग की है कि या तो फॉरेस्ट को इनसर्किल कर लो या फिर किसानों के खेतों को इनसर्किल करने के लिए जालीदार तार लगाने के लिए कम से कम 50 परसेंट सब्सिडी भारत सरकार दे और 50 परसेंट शेयर पंजाब सरकार दे तो मैं समझता हूं कि किसान भी बच जाएगा और जंगली जानवरों से भी बचाव हो पाएगा। मैं एक बार फिर मैं माननीय मंत्री जी का धन्यवाद करता हूं जिन्होंने विकास के लिए रिलेक्सेशन देकर बैलेंस तरीके से इनवायरमेंट के लिए काम किया है।

*SHRI T.G. VENKATESH BABU (CHENNAI NORTH): Though we have a separate ministry of Environment and Forest, the environmental situation in India is very pathetic. This is an area where we have failed miserably.

Air pollution in our country has gone from bad to worse. The Indian cities, which are almost 1/4th of the world cities are the worse affected through the industrial pollution, lack of waste management, transportation vehicles, etc.

The Bhopal gas tragedy of 1984 is not only the world's worst industrial disaster, but also one of the longest one going cover up 30 years on, the relief and adequate compensation to the victims of this accident is still eluding. The disastrous gas leakage in which nearly 25,000 people died and 1.5 lakh still continue to suffer from chronic illnesses. Many of them have been blinded forever. This is a classic case in which the industrial safeguards are proved to be the worst causality and in which the then Indian Government succumbed to the pressures of the MNCs. For the lack of a fool proof liability act, the US union carbide company was enabled to escape from its responsibility to the victims of the accidents.

The present Government does not seem to have learnt lessons from the Bhopal gas tragedy. The Nuclear Liability Act has been recently rendered void through a mechanism by which the international principle of "Polluter pays" is given up. Instead the Government and its agencies will pay the full compensation.

Traditional fuels like cow-dung cake and firewood kill lakhs of people every year through their poisonous fumes. Burning bio-mass as cooking fuel accounts for 3 times the carbon air pollution as all other air pollutants put together, including traffic fumes and industrial smoke. Thanks to the air pollution, Indians have 30% lower lung function than the Europeans. Every year there are 6.27 lakh premature deaths in India due to air pollution apart from the pollution related diseases like heart ailments, cardio-vascular affliction, etc. The pollution arising out of the traffic fumes in urban areas has devastating effects. Still we could not draw adequate parameters to check it. The CNGs used in Delhi vehicles as a pure and alternate fuel has not been carried through like all other experiments.

The Swachch Bharat Mission a cleanliness drive by the Government is welcome. But unless adequate measures are effected for waste disposal through recyclability and biodegradability, creating cleanliness fund involving corporates also, this Mission will end up as yet another publicity stunt. The cleanliness is related to poor conditions. For example, the open defecation which is also a slur on the country's pride can be abolished through providing adequate toilets only. Cleanliness is a luxury for the poor and not to be clean is not their choice.

The conservation of forests along with the species there is most required to maintain the eco system. Rebalancing the ecosystem will have disastrous consequences. Linear infrastructural projects like roads, railway tracks and power lines that make long intrusions into forests are a new threat to our forests, in addition to submergence by dams or clearance for mines. The norms for such projects are gradually been subjected to dilution which may lead to severe destruction of forests, massive landslides, erosion of the soil and finally destruction of the fragile ecosystem. So, a right balance is to be struck between development and protection of ecology, which will be sustainable in the longer run.

Soil conservation is another important issue. Intensification of farming in the last century led to soil erosion. The genetically modified crops are one such phenomena of intensified farming. GM crops are not sustainable due to fast erosion of the soil, though they may yield huge profits in the initial stages. The International Agency of Research on cancer, a respected arm of UNO declared recently that the two insecticides malathion and diazinon used in the GM crops and the glyphostate in herbicide of Mansanto, in the brand name of Round Up cause cancer. So, the Tamil Nadu Government under the guidance of Madam has banned the entry of GM crops into Tamil Nadu. Even the field trials are not permitted. The UN Food and Agricultural Organization has come out which a finding that because of soil destruction, the world is on an average, has just 60 more years of growing crops. Every year 12 million hectares of cultivatable land is lost through soil degradation. Crop rotation, the use of organic fertilizers and ecologically informed technology grouped together, known as agroecology, can effectively reduce the use of chemicals and soil degradation.

Tamil Nadu Government effectively prevented the Methane project which would have converted the whole Cauvery delta into a desert. DMK which brought the project under its rule, with the permission from the Center in which it was a partner, has now to oppose the project due to the stiff resistance from the farmers.

In a brilliant sunny country like ours, we seem to have largely ignored renewable sources like solar power and wind power. Even biomass fuels like dung can be used to produce biogas, a cleaner and more efficient fuel. T. Nadu Government has achieved the distinction of being in the forefront of producing renewable energy. It has been complemented by the Central Government for this remarkable achievement.

Another major environmental issue is the most threatening global warming. If the global temperature is allowed to exceed the threshold limit of 2°c temperature, then the world will face catastrophic consequences. If the outcome of the Lima climate conference is any indication, in all likelihood, the agreement on the Paris summit in December 2015 will be a weak and seriously compensated one that will lead to 3°c rise by the turn of the century, with developing countries bearing the brunt of the effects of severe climate change. The equity principle adopted at the first Kyoto Protocol will be seriously eroded and the developed countries will escape from the hook and evade from their historical responsibility for ever.

"The common but differentiated responsibility and respective capabilities" principle adopted in the Kyoto protocol envisages that the industrialist countries which have polluted the atmosphere to the maximum have the historical responsibility to redeem it, when the other countries have common responsibility to mitigate the carbon storage. The major carbon emitter, the USA is the only country which rejected the Kyoto protocol. US is consistently rejecting any legally binding commitments and is virtually doing everything to demolish the Kyoto protocol. The advanced countries will grab most of the atmospheric space leaving developing countries little room for growth. The principle of the equity is rudely discorded. Instead voluntary pledges as pushed by the US are to be the basis of Paris agreement from 2020 onwards. Current low pledges by US and the developed countries are certain to lead the planet to 3°-4° c.

Voluntary pledges are the main basis of Intended Nationally Determined Contributions (INDCs), a new alternate formulae thrust by US and its conglomerates. These INDCs are not to include the related element of financial contributions and technology transfer to assist the developing countries in their mitigation and adaptation actions in the post 2020 period.

The core principles of Kyoto protocol are included in the adopted text and its seems to have satisfied all the parties in the Lima conference. India's minister for environment and forests has gone on record that all our concerns had been addressed and we got what we wanted. But the reality is not so. "in the light of different national circumstances" - phrase is added to the Common but Differentiated Responsibility principle of Kyoto protocol, leaving room for various interpretations, that suits one. This distortion is also found in the US - China bilateral agreement also. So it is clear that the emerging agreement is going to be centered around INDCs (Intended National Determined Contributions). The U.S is adopting a deviated course of entering into bilateral agreements on climate change which China and India instead of the unviable unilateral approach it adopted so far. This move is to nullify any multilateral agreement reached which will not be at the interest of US. Like China, India also seems to have treaded on this dangerous collusion with US. Developing countries like China and India have failed to lead from the front and betrayed the under developed countries.

The current per capita Green House Gas emission level for China is above 6.5 tonnes of CO2 equivalent, compared with 17.6 tonnes for the US and according to estimates, it will be around 12-14 tonnes by its peaking year in 2030, similar to US per capita income. This is way above the two tonne limit required to limit the average temperature increase to 2°c. 

Ultimately the apparent success of the Lima conference from the perspective of the developing countries is only symbolic. The original draft is improved only in form but not in substance. Developing countries, particularly the poor and vulnerable ones, which are already facing the impacts of 0.85°c increase since industrialization began, will bear the brunt of the disastrous effects of severe climate change. Kolkata, Chennai and Mumbai the seaside metropolis of India are facing the threat of submersion, since the total increase in sea level in the 20th century is 0.17 meter.

Hence Indian government has to find an alternative path to overcome the disaster of environmental and climate neglects.

योगी आदित्यनाथ (गोरखपुर): सभापति महोदय, पर्यावरण, वन एवं जलवायु परिवर्तन मंत्रालय की अनुदान की मांगों का समर्थन करने के लिए मैं खड़ा हुआ हूं।

यह एक महत्वपूर्ण मंत्रालय है और वर्तमान की चुनौतियों और विकास के बीच में किस प्रकार से साम्यता लायी जाए, यह भी एक गंभीर मुद्दा है, जिसको उन्हें देखना है। इस मंत्रालय के अंतर्गत वनस्पति, जीव-जंतु, वन और वन्य जीवों के संरक्षण और सर्वेक्षण का, प्रदू­ाण की रोकथाम और उसके नियंत्रण, वनरोपण और उसकी पुनरूत्पत्ति, पर्यावरण संरक्षण तथा पशुओं के कल्याण आदि से संबंधित महत्वपूर्ण जिम्मेदारी है। 

16.45 hrs (Hon. Deputy Speaker in the Chair)

महोदय, जलवायु परिवर्तन एक महत्वपूर्ण मुद्दा है। इसके दो प्रमुख कारण हैं- एक प्राकृतिक कारण है और दूसरा मानवीय कारण है। अंधाधुंध वनों की कटाई, अवैज्ञानिक विकास की सोच और परिवहन तंत्र के कारण भी वायुमंडलीय उत्सर्जन के कारण भी वायुमंडल में गैस और एरोसौल्स एकत्रित हो जाते हैं, जिसने ग्रीन हाऊस इफेक्ट की स्थिति पैदा की है और इससे धरती का तापमान भी बढ़ा है। ग्लोबल वार्मिंग हम सबके सामने एक चुनौती है क्योंकि समुद्र के जलस्तर का बढ़ना, चक्रवाती तूफानों में तेजी आना, आज पूरा उत्तर भारत बेमौसम बारिश और ओलावृ­िट की चपेट में है। किसानों की फसलें उससे प्रभावित हुई हैं। भारत जैसे विकासशील देश के लिए यह ग्लोबल वार्मिंग और क्लाइमेट चेंज अपने-आप में एक गंभीर चुनौती बनकर आया है। हम सबके सामने महत्वपूर्ण चुनौती यह है कि लगातार वनों का क्षेत्रफल घटा है। कभी यह रेशियो 60 : 40 का था, आज इस देश में मात्र 23 प्रतिशत भौगोलिक क्षेत्रफल ही वनों से आच्छादित है। स्वाभाविक रूप से पर्यावरण के सामने यह एक गंभीर चुनौती है और ये एक-दूसरे से जुड़े हुए हैं। वन, पर्यावरण और जलवायु परिवर्तन हैं, इनको हम एक-दूसरे से अलग करके नहीं रख सकते हैं। जो अच्छी बातें सामने आयी हैं, वे ये हैं कि अगले पाँच व­ाऩ के लिए ग्रीन एनर्जी प्रोजेक्ट के लिए मंत्रालय के द्वारा एक प्रयास प्रारंभ हुआ है कि 1.7 लाख करोड़ रुपये सरकारी बैंकों से सोलर और विंड एनर्जी पर खर्च करने के लिए जो व्यवस्था की गयी है, मुझे लगता है कि इससे लगभग 34 हजार मेगावाट बिजली का उत्पादन हो सकता है। आज सुबह ही माननीय मंत्री जी ने यहाँ पर कहा कि सरकार का टारगेट व­ाऩ 2022 तक एक लाख मेगावाट सोलर एनर्जी का प्रोडक्शन और लगभग 60 हजार मेगावाट विंड एनर्जी के प्रोडक्शन का लक्ष्य रखा गया है। स्वाभाविक रूप से इससे कोल पर निर्भरता कम होगी और उसका प्रभाव पर्यावरण के लिए अनुकूल होगा क्योंकि जब हम कोल पर निर्भरता कम करेंगे तो उतना ही हमारे लिए अच्छी स्थिति होगी। ग्लोबल वार्मिंग हम सबके सामने एक चुनौती है। यदि समय रहते हमने इस पर नियंत्रण नहीं किया तो दुनिया की बड़ी आबादी भुखमरी की चपेट में आने वाली है और इसका सर्वाधिक दु­प्रभाव भारत जैसे विकासशील देश पर पड़ने वाला है क्योंकि आज भी तमाम प्रयासों के बावजूद देश में गरीबी की स्थिति 32 प्रतिशत तक बनी हुई है। 

हम विकास की बात तो कर रहे हैं, लेकिन विकास के चलते इस देश के अंदर तापमान में वृद्धि की बात आ रही है। उस पर भी हमें अवश्य विचार करना चाहिए और इसीलिए मैं माननीय मंत्री जी का ध्यान उन मुद्दों की ओर आकर्­िात करना चाहूंगा, जो हाल में ही खास तौर से अभी हम लोगों को देखने को मिले हैं। हमारे हिमालयन क्षेत्र ने अभी दो व­ाऩ पूर्व केदारनाथ में उत्तराखण्ड की त्रासदी को झेला है। अभी पूरा उत्तर भारत जलवायु परिवर्तन, जिसमें अति वृ­िट, ओलावृ­िट की परिस्थितियों को किसानों को झेलने के लिए मजबूर होना पड़ा है। नेपाल में 25 अप्रैल को आये हुए भूकम्प की त्रासदी से न केवल उत्तर भारत, बल्कि पूरा नेपाल आज तबाही की कहानी रच रहा है। मैं माननीय मंत्री जी से अनुरोध करना चाहूंगा कि हिमालयन परिक्षेत्र के पर्यावरण के बारे में अवश्य विचार होना चाहिए क्योंकि अगर हिमालय की परिस्थिति के वि­ाय को अभी से हम लोगों ने गंभीरता से नहीं लिया तो भारत के उत्तरी क्षेत्र के लिए हिमालय से आने वाली सदानीरा नदियों के कारण रेगिस्तान बनने का खतरा आने वाले समय में पैदा हो सकता है। 

माननीय प्रधानमंत्री जी द्वारा नमामि गंगे के रूप में गंगा की अविरलता और निर्मलता के बारे में जो बातें कही हैं, गंगा की अविरलता और निर्मलता के लिए आवश्यक है कि गंगा और उसकी सहायक नदियों को हम प्रदू­ाण से मुक्त रखें और उनकी अविरलता को बनाए रखें। उसके लिए वहां से जितनी नदिया आती हैं, मैं पूर्वी उत्तर प्रदेश को देखता हूं, वहां पर आमी नदी, रोहिनी नदी, क्वानो नदी आदि सभी नदियां पूरी तरह से प्रदू­िात हो चुकी हैं, उनका जल पीने लायक नहीं है, लेकिन राज्य सरकार का प्रदू­ाण नियंत्रण बोर्ड प्रभावी भूमिका का निर्वाह नहीं कर पा रहा है। जब तक हम लोग उद्योगों का कचरा नदियों में जाने से नहीं रोकेंगे, जो ट्रीटमेंट प्लांट लगाए जाते हैं, उनका उपयोग नहीं होता है। हमारी नगरपालिकाओं ने वाटर ट्रीटमेंट प्लांट या तो लगाए नहीं हैं, अगर लगाए हैं तो उनका उपयोग नहीं कर पाती हैं और पूरा कचरा नदियों में जाता है जिससे नदियों का जल प्रदू­िात होता है। हमें इन नदियों की अविरलता और निर्मलता के लिए ट्रीटमेंट प्लांट की कार्रवाई को करना होगा क्योंकि जल प्रदू­ाण तमाम प्रकार की जलजनित बीमारियों का कारण बन रहा है। प्रति व­ाऩ पूर्वी उत्तर प्रदेश में हम लोग हजारों बच्चों को इंसेफेलाइटिस बीमारी की वजह से खोते हैं। इस बीमारी का जो नया वि­ााणु वर्तमान में चिन्हित हुआ है, उसका कारण प्रदू­िात जल है। राज्य सरकार की प्रदू­ाण के लिए बनाई गयी इकाइयां और बोर्ड हैं, उनको प्रभावी भूमिका निभानी होगी। 

प्राकृतिक झीलों के संरक्षण के लिए जो एनएलसीपी की योजना है, गोरखपुर में रामगढ़ ताल परियोजना के लिए वन एवं पर्यावरण मंत्रालय ने कुछ राशि उपलब्ध कराई थी। उसी प्रकार से, रामगढ़ ताल की तर्ज पर बखिरा झील है, महेशरा ताल है, इन सभी के संरक्षण की भी योजना इसमें बनाई जाए।...(व्यवधान)
